114	// Open opens (or creates) sessions.db for writing — a single serialized connection,
115	// applying WAL + performance pragmas (matching pkg/provenance) and ensuring the schema
116	// exists. Use OpenReader for the read-only interactive browse path.
117	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
118		return openWith(path, writerConns)
119	}
120	
121	// OpenReader opens sessions.db for the interactive browse path (resume/search), which
122	// only reads. It allows several concurrent connections so one slow full-text query can't
123	// starve the UI (WAL permits many simultaneous readers). Never write through this handle.
124	func OpenReader(path string) (*Store, error) {
125		return openWith(path, readerConns)
126	}
127	
128	func openWith(path string, maxConns int) (*Store, error) {
129		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
130			return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating database directory: %w", err)
131		}
132	
133		s, err := openStore(path, maxConns)
134		if err == nil {
135			return s, nil
136		}
137	
138		// A disk-I/O error opening the index almost always means STALE WAL sidecars: the main
139		// sessions.db was deleted or replaced while sessions.db-wal / sessions.db-shm were left behind,
140		// so SQLite fails trying to recover a WAL that no longer matches the file (e.g. a short read,
141		// SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ / 522). The sidecars are ephemeral and sessions.db is a derived cache
142		// (rebuilt by reindex), so clearing the sidecars and retrying once is safe and never loses real
143		// data — it just avoids a hard failure that forces the user to hunt down the sidecar files.
144		if isDiskIOError(err) {
145			slog.Warn("sessions.db open failed with disk I/O error; clearing stale WAL sidecars and retrying", "error", err)
146			removeWALSidecars(path)
147			return openStore(path, maxConns)
148		}
149		return nil, err
150	}

152	// openStore opens sessions.db with the connection pragmas and ensures the schema exists.
153	func openStore(path string, maxConns int) (*Store, error) {
154		dsn := "file:" + filepath.ToSlash(path) + "?_pragma=" + strings.Join(connectionPragmas, "&_pragma=")
155		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
156		if err != nil {
157			return nil, fmt.Errorf("opening sessions.db: %w", err)
158		}
159	
160		db.SetMaxOpenConns(maxConns)
161		db.SetMaxIdleConns(maxConns)
162	
163		s := &Store{db: db}
164		if err := s.ensureSchema(); err != nil {
165			_ = db.Close()
166			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ensuring schema: %w", err)
167		}
168		return s, nil
169	}

171	// isDiskIOError reports whether err is (or wraps) a SQLite disk-I/O error — the SQLITE_IOERR
172	// family (primary result code 10), which includes extended codes like SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ
173	// (522) that a stale WAL sidecar produces.
174	func isDiskIOError(err error) bool {
175		const sqliteIOErr = 10 // SQLITE_IOERR primary code; extended codes are 10 | (n<<8)
176		var sqliteErr *sqlite.Error
177		if errors.As(err, &sqliteErr) {
178			return sqliteErr.Code()&0xFF == sqliteIOErr
179		}
180		return false
181	}

183	// removeWALSidecars deletes sessions.db's WAL/shm sidecar files. Best-effort: a missing file is
184	// fine, and any other removal error is logged but not fatal (the retry open will surface it).
185	func removeWALSidecars(path string) {

188				slog.Warn("failed to remove WAL sidecar", "path", path+suffix, "error", err)
189			}
190		}
191	}

260		// picker via the resume/search TUI. Rather than dropping the row — which reindex would
261		// simply re-add on the next pass — we keep the row, flag it deleted, and strip its FTS
262		// body. Every read path filters deleted=0, the write path (upsertOne) refuses to
263		// resurrect a tombstoned row even on new content, and reindex skips it. So a delete
264		// stays deleted until the user wipes sessions.db and rebuilds. Benign error when the
265		// column already exists. Constant DEFAULT keeps existing rows visible (0). See
266		// docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
267		s.runMigration(`ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN deleted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`)
268		// Drop the old single-column project index now superseded by the composite
269		// idx_sessions_project_recent (project_id is its left prefix). Idempotent; a no-op
270		// on fresh databases that never had it.
271		s.runMigration(`DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_sessions_project`)
272		return nil
273	}
274	
275	// runMigration applies an idempotent schema migration whose error is usually the benign
276	// "column/index already exists". We can't cleanly tell that apart from a real failure (locked
277	// DB, I/O) without matching driver-specific strings, so we log at Debug rather than fail: a
278	// genuine problem still resurfaces as a later query error, but it is no longer fully invisible.
279	func (s *Store) runMigration(stmt string) {
280		if _, err := s.db.Exec(stmt); err != nil {
281			slog.Debug("sessionindex: migration step skipped", "stmt", stmt, "error", err)
282		}
283	}
284	
285	// Fingerprints returns the freshness fingerprint of every indexed session, keyed by
286	// fingerprintKey(agent, session_id). reindex loads this once and skips any session
287	// whose native file is unchanged (same size + mtime) and was indexed by the current
288	// logic version.
289	func (s *Store) Fingerprints() (map[string]Fingerprint, error) {
290		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT agent, session_id, size, mtime, index_version, deleted FROM sessions`)
291		if err != nil {
292			return nil, err
293		}
294		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
295	
296		out := make(map[string]Fingerprint)
297		for rows.Next() {
298			var agent, sessionID string
299			var deleted int
300			var fp Fingerprint
301			if err := rows.Scan(&agent, &sessionID, &fp.Size, &fp.Mtime, &fp.Version, &deleted); err != nil {
302				return nil, err
303			}
304			fp.Deleted = deleted != 0
305			out[FingerprintKey(agent, sessionID)] = fp
306		}
307		return out, rows.Err()
308	}
309	
310	// FingerprintKey is the map key for a session's fingerprint: agent + NUL + session_id.
311	func FingerprintKey(agent, sessionID string) string {
312		return agent + "\x00" + sessionID
313	}
314	
315	// sessionUpsertStmts are the per-row statements UpsertBatch prepares once and reuses across
316	// every row in a transaction, so the SQL is parsed once per batch instead of once per row.
317	type sessionUpsertStmts struct {
318		insSession    *sql.Stmt
319		selOldRowid   *sql.Stmt
320		delFTSByRowid *sql.Stmt
321		delFTSByKey   *sql.Stmt
322		insFTS        *sql.Stmt
323	}
324	
325	// upsertOne writes one session's row and full-text row using the batch's prepared statements.
326	// FTS5 standalone tables are not auto-synced, so the FTS row is maintained by hand. The new FTS
327	// row is inserted first so its rowid can be stored on the sessions row (fts_rowid) — that link
328	// is what makes later body reads and replace-deletes O(1) rowid lookups instead of whole-FTS
329	// scans (session_id/agent are UNINDEXED). For an existing session the prior FTS row is removed
330	// first; brand-new sessions (sess.IsNew) skip that lookup-and-delete entirely.
331	func upsertOne(st sessionUpsertStmts, sess Session) error {
332		if !sess.IsNew {
333			ex, err := lookupExisting(st, sess)
334			if err != nil {
335				return err
336			}
337			// A soft-deleted session stays deleted even when new turns arrive: skip the write
338			// entirely so the tombstone (and its stripped FTS body) survives. This covers every
339			// writer — reindex, the live `run`/`watch` indexer, and `sync` — so a delete only
340			// comes back after a full sessions.db wipe + reindex. See the deleted-column migration.
341			if ex.deleted {
342				return nil
343			}
344			if ex.found {
345				if err := clearOldFTSRow(st, sess, ex.ftsRowid); err != nil {
346					return err
347				}
348			}
349		}
350		res, err := st.insFTS.Exec(sess.SessionID, sess.Agent, sess.Name, sess.Body)
351		if err != nil {
352			return fmt.Errorf("insert fts row: %w", err)
353		}
354		ftsRowid, err := res.LastInsertId()
355		if err != nil {
356			return fmt.Errorf("read fts rowid: %w", err)
357		}
358		if _, err := st.insSession.Exec(
359			sess.ProjectID, sess.ProjectName, sess.Agent, sess.SessionID, sess.CreatedAt, sess.UpdatedAt,
360			sess.UserTurns, sess.TotalTurns, sess.Slug, sess.Name, sess.NativePath, sess.OriginCwd,
361			sess.Size, sess.Mtime, sess.IndexVersion, sess.IndexedAt, ftsRowid); err != nil {
362			return fmt.Errorf("upsert session row: %w", err)
363		}
364		return nil
365	}
366	
367	// existingRow is the prior index state for a session: its FTS rowid link (if any) and whether
368	// it is a soft-delete tombstone. found is false when there is no prior sessions row at all.
369	type existingRow struct {
370		ftsRowid sql.NullInt64
371		deleted  bool
372		found    bool
373	}
374	
375	// lookupExisting resolves the prior sessions row for sess by primary key, reporting its FTS
376	// rowid link and tombstone flag. It is the single read upsertOne needs before writing: a
377	// tombstoned row must not be resurrected, and a live row's stale FTS row must be cleared first.
378	func lookupExisting(st sessionUpsertStmts, sess Session) (existingRow, error) {
379		var ex existingRow
380		var deleted int
381		switch err := st.selOldRowid.QueryRow(sess.Agent, sess.SessionID).Scan(&ex.ftsRowid, &deleted); {
382		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
383			return ex, nil // no prior row
384		case err != nil:
385			return ex, fmt.Errorf("look up existing session: %w", err)
386		}
387		ex.found = true
388		ex.deleted = deleted != 0
389		return ex, nil
390	}
391	
392	// clearOldFTSRow removes an existing session's current FTS row before the sessions row is
393	// replaced (INSERT OR REPLACE would otherwise drop the fts_rowid link and orphan the FTS row).
394	// It uses the already-resolved fts_rowid (O(1)); for rows written before fts_rowid existed
395	// (NULL) it falls back to the by-key delete — a whole-FTS scan that a reindex retires by
396	// repopulating fts_rowid.
397	func clearOldFTSRow(st sessionUpsertStmts, sess Session, ftsRowid sql.NullInt64) error {
398		if ftsRowid.Valid {
399			if _, err := st.delFTSByRowid.Exec(ftsRowid.Int64); err != nil {
400				return fmt.Errorf("clear fts row by rowid: %w", err)
401			}
402			return nil
403		}
404		if _, err := st.delFTSByKey.Exec(sess.Agent, sess.SessionID); err != nil {
405			return fmt.Errorf("clear legacy fts row: %w", err)
406		}
407		return nil
408	}
409	
410	// prepareUpsert prepares the per-row statements on tx and returns them with a closer.
411	func prepareUpsert(tx *sql.Tx) (sessionUpsertStmts, func(), error) {
412		var prepared []*sql.Stmt
413		closer := func() {
414			for _, s := range prepared {
415				_ = s.Close()
416			}
417		}
418		prep := func(what, query string) (*sql.Stmt, error) {
419			s, err := tx.Prepare(query)
420			if err != nil {
421				closer()
422				return nil, fmt.Errorf("prepare %s: %w", what, err)
423			}
424			prepared = append(prepared, s)
425			return s, nil
426		}
427	
428		insSession, err := prep("session upsert", `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sessions (`+sessionInsertColumns+`)
429			VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`)
430		if err != nil {
431			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
432		}
433		selOldRowid, err := prep("existing row lookup", `SELECT fts_rowid, deleted FROM sessions WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`)
434		if err != nil {
435			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
436		}
437		delFTSByRowid, err := prep("fts delete by rowid", `DELETE FROM sessions_fts WHERE rowid = ?`)
438		if err != nil {
439			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
440		}
441		delFTSByKey, err := prep("fts delete by key", `DELETE FROM sessions_fts WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`)
442		if err != nil {
443			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
444		}
445		insFTS, err := prep("fts insert", `INSERT INTO sessions_fts (session_id, agent, name, body) VALUES (?,?,?,?)`)
446		if err != nil {
447			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
448		}
449		return sessionUpsertStmts{
450			insSession:    insSession,
451			selOldRowid:   selOldRowid,
452			delFTSByRowid: delFTSByRowid,
453			delFTSByKey:   delFTSByKey,
454			insFTS:        insFTS,
455		}, closer, nil
456	}
457	
458	// Upsert inserts or replaces a single session row and its full-text row, atomically. A
459	// re-index of the same session (same agent + session_id) replaces both in lockstep.
460	func (s *Store) Upsert(sess Session) error {
461		return s.UpsertBatch([]Session{sess})
462	}
463	
464	// UpsertBatch writes many sessions in one transaction — the write path for `reindex`,
465	// which batches to avoid thousands of tiny WAL commits.
466	func (s *Store) UpsertBatch(sessions []Session) error {
467		if len(sessions) == 0 {
468			return nil
469		}
470		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
471		if err != nil {
472			return fmt.Errorf("begin upsert: %w", err)
473		}
474		committed := false
475		defer func() {
476			if !committed {
477				_ = tx.Rollback()
478			}
479		}()
480	
481		st, closeStmts, err := prepareUpsert(tx)
482		if err != nil {
483			return err
484		}
485		defer closeStmts()
486	
487		for _, sess := range sessions {
488			if err := upsertOne(st, sess); err != nil {
489				return err
490			}
491		}
492	
493		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
494			return fmt.Errorf("commit upsert: %w", err)
495		}
496		committed = true
497		return nil
498	}
499	
500	// SoftDeleteSession tombstones a single session: flags the sessions row deleted and strips its
501	// FTS body, so it vanishes from the picker and search but the row survives as a fingerprint that
502	// reindex/warm skip forever (see the deleted-column migration and upsertOne's tombstone guard).
503	// The native session file on disk is untouched. Must be called on a writer handle (Open, not
504	// OpenReader). Returns the number of rows affected (0 when the session isn't indexed).
505	func (s *Store) SoftDeleteSession(agent, sessionID string) (int, error) {
506		return s.softDelete(`agent = ? AND session_id = ?`, agent, sessionID)
507	}
508	
509	// SoftDeleteProject tombstones every session in a project (see SoftDeleteSession). Future
510	// sessions in the same project are NOT blocked — a fresh session there indexes normally; only
511	// the rows that exist at delete time are tombstoned. Returns the number of rows affected.
512	func (s *Store) SoftDeleteProject(projectID string) (int, error) {
513		return s.softDelete(`project_id = ?`, projectID)
514	}
515	
516	// softDelete flags the rows matched by where (deleted = 1) and clears their FTS rows in one
517	// transaction, keeping each sessions row (and its fingerprint) so reindex treats it as
518	// unchanged. FTS rows are removed by (agent, session_id) — the same by-key delete upsert uses,
519	// which works on the UNINDEXED FTS columns without relying on row-value subquery support in
520	// FTS5. Only already-live rows are touched (deleted = 0), so a re-delete is a no-op returning 0.
521	func (s *Store) softDelete(where string, args ...any) (int, error) {
522		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
523		if err != nil {
524			return 0, fmt.Errorf("begin soft delete: %w", err)
525		}
526		committed := false
527		defer func() {
528			if !committed {
529				_ = tx.Rollback()
530			}
531		}()
532	
533		// Resolve exactly which sessions this delete targets, so the FTS rows can be cleared by key.
534		rows, err := tx.Query(`SELECT agent, session_id FROM sessions WHERE (`+where+`) AND deleted = 0`, args...)
535		if err != nil {
536			return 0, fmt.Errorf("select rows to delete: %w", err)
537		}
538		type key struct{ agent, sessionID string }
539		var targets []key
540		for rows.Next() {
541			var k key
542			if err := rows.Scan(&k.agent, &k.sessionID); err != nil {
543				_ = rows.Close()
544				return 0, fmt.Errorf("scan row to delete: %w", err)
545			}
546			targets = append(targets, k)
547		}
548		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
549			_ = rows.Close()
550			return 0, fmt.Errorf("iterate rows to delete: %w", err)
551		}
552		_ = rows.Close()
553	
554		for _, k := range targets {
555			if _, err := tx.Exec(`DELETE FROM sessions_fts WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`, k.agent, k.sessionID); err != nil {
556				return 0, fmt.Errorf("clear fts row: %w", err)
557			}
558		}
559	
560		if _, err := tx.Exec(`UPDATE sessions SET deleted = 1, fts_rowid = NULL WHERE (`+where+`) AND deleted = 0`, args...); err != nil {
561			return 0, fmt.Errorf("tombstone sessions: %w", err)
562		}
563	
564		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
565			return 0, fmt.Errorf("commit soft delete: %w", err)
566		}
567		committed = true
568		return len(targets), nil
569	}
570	
571	// Exists reports whether a session row is already indexed, looked up by the primary key
572	// (agent, session_id) so it stays O(log n) instead of scanning. Because a session's sessions
573	// row and its sessions_fts row are always written together (upsertOne, one transaction), a
574	// missing sessions row guarantees a missing FTS row — which lets the live writer set
575	// Session.IsNew and skip the whole-table FTS delete for genuinely new sessions.
576	func (s *Store) Exists(agent, sessionID string) (bool, error) {
577		var one int
578		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`, agent, sessionID).Scan(&one)
579		if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
580			return false, nil
581		}
582		if err != nil {
583			return false, err
584		}
585		return true, nil
586	}
587	
588	// Count returns the number of indexed sessions.
589	func (s *Store) Count() (int, error) {
590		var n int
591		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE deleted = 0`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
592			return 0, err
593		}
594		return n, nil
595	}
596	
597	// ProjectCount returns the number of distinct attributed projects in the index
598	// (excluding the unknownID bucket).
599	func (s *Store) ProjectCount(unknownID string) (int, error) {
600		var n int
601		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT project_id) FROM sessions WHERE project_id != ? AND deleted = 0`, unknownID).Scan(&n)
602		return n, err
603	}
604	
605	// UnattributedCount returns the number of sessions in the unknownID bucket.
606	func (s *Store) UnattributedCount(unknownID string) (int, error) {
607		var n int
608		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE project_id = ? AND deleted = 0`, unknownID).Scan(&n)
609		return n, err
610	}
611	
612	// KnownCwds returns the distinct non-empty origin_cwd values across all live indexed sessions —
613	// every working directory the index has ever learned, including those captured in real time by
614	// run/watch/sync. reindex's Cursor cwd-recovery seeds its md5(cwd)→cwd map with these (read before
615	// it upserts) so a Cursor session keeps the project attribution the live path recorded, instead of
616	// having reindex re-derive it from a cwd-less global enumeration and clobber it to "unknown".
617	func (s *Store) KnownCwds() ([]string, error) {
618		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT DISTINCT origin_cwd FROM sessions WHERE origin_cwd != '' AND deleted = 0`)
619		if err != nil {
620			return nil, err
621		}
622		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
623	
624		var cwds []string
625		for rows.Next() {
626			var cwd string
627			if err := rows.Scan(&cwd); err != nil {
628				return nil, err
629			}
630			cwds = append(cwds, cwd)
631		}
632		return cwds, rows.Err()
633	}
634	
635	// GetSession returns the LIVE indexed session for (agent, sessionID), or ok=false when there is
636	// no such row — never indexed, OR soft-deleted (deleted = 0 is required, unlike Exists). Body is
637	// not populated. Used by resume's selection-time guard to prefer an in-place local resume over a
638	// cloud fetch when a cloud-badged session is actually present on this machine.
639	func (s *Store) GetSession(agent, sessionID string) (Session, bool, error) {
640		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT `+sessionColumns+`
641			FROM sessions WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ? AND deleted = 0`, agent, sessionID)
642		if err != nil {
643			return Session{}, false, err
644		}
645		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
646	
647		sessions, err := scanSessions(rows)
648		if err != nil {
649			return Session{}, false, err
650		}
651		if len(sessions) == 0 {
652			return Session{}, false, nil
653		}
654		return sessions[0], true, nil
655	}
656	
657	// ListByProject returns a project's sessions, newest activity first. Body is not
658	// populated (it lives only in the FTS index). Used by the `specstory resume` picker.
659	func (s *Store) ListByProject(projectID string) ([]Session, error) {
660		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT `+sessionColumns+`
661			FROM sessions WHERE project_id = ? AND deleted = 0 ORDER BY updated_at DESC, created_at DESC`, projectID)
662		if err != nil {
663			return nil, err
664		}
665		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
666		return scanSessions(rows)
667	}
668	
669	// ProjectSummary is a rolled-up view of one project for the all-projects picker.
670	type ProjectSummary struct {
671		ProjectID    string
672		ProjectName  string
673		Sessions     int            // total sessions in the project
674		LastActivity string         // most recent updated_at across the project
675		AgentCounts  map[string]int // sessions per agent (claude, codex, …)
676	
677		// IsCloud marks a project that exists only in SpecStory Cloud (from another machine, never
678		// worked on locally). Set only on cloud-blended rows in the all-projects browser; local
679		// rollups leave it false. AgentCounts is nil for these (the cloud list has no per-agent
680		// breakdown).
681		IsCloud bool
682	}
683	
684	// ListProjects returns one rolled-up summary per project, most recently active first.
685	// Used by the all-projects view (date-bucketed). The unknown-project bucket is included;
686	// the caller decides how to present it.
687	func (s *Store) ListProjects() ([]ProjectSummary, error) {
688		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT project_id, project_name, agent, COUNT(*), MAX(updated_at)
689			FROM sessions WHERE deleted = 0 GROUP BY project_id, agent`)
690		if err != nil {
691			return nil, err
692		}
693		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
694	
695		byID := map[string]*ProjectSummary{}
696		for rows.Next() {
697			var pid, pname, agent, last string
698			var n int
699			if err := rows.Scan(&pid, &pname, &agent, &n, &last); err != nil {
700				return nil, err
701			}
702			ps, ok := byID[pid]
703			if !ok {
704				ps = &ProjectSummary{ProjectID: pid, ProjectName: pname, AgentCounts: map[string]int{}}
705				byID[pid] = ps
706			}
707			ps.Sessions += n
708			ps.AgentCounts[agent] += n
709			if ps.ProjectName == "" {
710				ps.ProjectName = pname
711			}
712			if last > ps.LastActivity {
713				ps.LastActivity = last
714			}
715		}
716		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
717			return nil, err
718		}
719	
720		out := make([]ProjectSummary, 0, len(byID))
721		for _, ps := range byID {
722			out = append(out, *ps)
723		}
724		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].LastActivity > out[j].LastActivity })
725		return out, nil
726	}
727	
728	// ProjectSessionKey identifies one local session within a project for the all-projects rollup
729	// merge: the (agent, session_id) fingerprint the cloud rows dedup against. No activity time
730	// rides along — the local rollup's LastActivity (from ListProjects) already carries it.
731	type ProjectSessionKey struct {
732		Agent     string // provider id: claude, codex, …
733		SessionID string // native session id
734	}
735	
736	// ListAllSessionKeysByProject returns every non-deleted local session keyed by project_id, for
737	// the all-projects browser's session-level merge with cloud rows. Unlike ListProjects (a
738	// rollup), this returns the per-session fingerprint set so the caller can dedup cloud rows against
739	// local by (agent, session_id) — local preferred — and recompute accurate per-agent chips / totals /
740	// last activity from the union. Used only by the cloud-projects blend; the local-only path keeps
741	// using ListProjects (a single grouped query is cheaper than enumerating then rolling up client-side).
742	func (s *Store) ListAllSessionKeysByProject() (map[string][]ProjectSessionKey, error) {
743		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT project_id, agent, session_id
744			FROM sessions WHERE deleted = 0`)
745		if err != nil {
746			return nil, err
747		}
748		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
749	
750		out := make(map[string][]ProjectSessionKey)
751		for rows.Next() {
752			var pid, agent, sid string
753			if err := rows.Scan(&pid, &agent, &sid); err != nil {
754				return nil, err
755			}
756			out[pid] = append(out[pid], ProjectSessionKey{Agent: agent, SessionID: sid})
757		}
758		return out, rows.Err()
759	}
760	
761	// SessionBody returns the full-text conversation body for a session (for the preview
762	// pane), or "" if the session has no indexed body (e.g. Cursor, metadata-only).
763	func (s *Store) SessionBody(agent, sessionID string) (string, error) {
764		var body string
765		// Fast path: resolve the FTS row by the rowid stored on the sessions row (O(1)), instead of
766		// scanning the whole FTS (session_id/agent are UNINDEXED).
767		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT f.body FROM sessions s
768			JOIN sessions_fts f ON f.rowid = s.fts_rowid
769			WHERE s.agent = ? AND s.session_id = ?`, agent, sessionID).Scan(&body)
770		if err == nil {
771			return body, nil
772		}
773		if !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
774			return "", err
775		}
776		// No fts_rowid link (a row written before the column existed). Fall back to the by-key scan;
777		// a reindex repopulates fts_rowid and retires this path.
778		err = s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT body FROM sessions_fts WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`,
779			agent, sessionID).Scan(&body)
780		if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
781			return "", nil
782		}
783		return body, err
784	}
785	
786	// Search runs a full-text query and returns matching sessions, most recent first.
787	// projectID scopes the search to one project; "" searches across all projects.
788	func (s *Store) Search(query, projectID string) ([]Session, error) {
789		return s.SearchContext(context.Background(), query, projectID)
790	}
791	
792	// SearchContext is Search bound to a context. The interactive search cancels the context
793	// when a newer keystroke arrives, which aborts a slow in-flight query and frees its
794	// connection. Snippets are deliberately fetched separately for only the visible rows:
795	// FTS5 snippet generation over hundreds of full transcripts dominates broad searches.
796	func (s *Store) SearchContext(ctx context.Context, query, projectID string) ([]Session, error) {
797		q := `SELECT ` + prefixed("s", sessionColumns) + `
798			FROM sessions_fts
799			JOIN sessions s ON s.agent = sessions_fts.agent AND s.session_id = sessions_fts.session_id
800			WHERE sessions_fts MATCH ? AND s.deleted = 0`
801		args := []any{query}
802		if projectID != "" {
803			q += ` AND s.project_id = ?`
804			args = append(args, projectID)
805		}
806		// Order by recency, not FTS5's BM25 rank. For full-conversation transcripts BM25 is
807		// noisy (length-normalization dominates) and a single-term query gets no IDF signal,
808		// so relevance order looks arbitrary; newest-first is what's useful when browsing your
809		// own history. It also makes LIMIT keep the 500 most RECENT matches (vs the 500 densest)
810		// and skips BM25 scoring entirely. updated_at is ISO 8601, so TEXT sort = chronological.
811		q += ` ORDER BY s.updated_at DESC LIMIT 500`
812	
813		rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, q, args...)
814		if err != nil {
815			return nil, err
816		}
817		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
818	
819		return scanSessions(rows)
820	}
821	
822	// Snippets returns highlighted match snippets for the provided sessions. The result is
823	// keyed by FingerprintKey(agent, session_id). Matched terms are wrapped in \x02 and \x03
824	// (STX/ETX) so callers can highlight without colliding with conversation text.
825	func (s *Store) Snippets(query string, sessions []Session) (map[string]string, error) {
826		return s.SnippetsContext(context.Background(), query, sessions)
827	}
828	
829	// SnippetsContext is Snippets bound to a context. Callers should pass only the currently
830	// visible rows; snippet() is intentionally lazy because it is the expensive part of FTS
831	// search on long transcripts.
832	func (s *Store) SnippetsContext(ctx context.Context, query string, sessions []Session) (map[string]string, error) {
833		out := map[string]string{}
834		if query == "" || len(sessions) == 0 {
835			return out, nil
836		}
837	
838		clauses := make([]string, 0, len(sessions))
839		args := []any{query}
840		seen := map[string]bool{}
841		for _, sess := range sessions {
842			key := FingerprintKey(sess.Agent, sess.SessionID)
843			if seen[key] {
844				continue
845			}
846			seen[key] = true
847			clauses = append(clauses, `(agent = ? AND session_id = ?)`)
848			args = append(args, sess.Agent, sess.SessionID)
849		}
850		if len(clauses) == 0 {
851			return out, nil
852		}
853	
854		q := `SELECT agent, session_id, snippet(sessions_fts, 3, char(2), char(3), '…', 12)
855			FROM sessions_fts
856			WHERE sessions_fts MATCH ? AND (` + strings.Join(clauses, ` OR `) + `)`
857		rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, q, args...)
858		if err != nil {
859			return nil, err
860		}
861		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
862	
863		for rows.Next() {
864			var agent, sessionID, snippet string
865			if err := rows.Scan(&agent, &sessionID, &snippet); err != nil {
866				return nil, err
867			}
868			out[FingerprintKey(agent, sessionID)] = snippet
869		}
870		return out, rows.Err()
871	}
872	
873	// prefixed qualifies each comma-separated column in cols with the given table alias,
874	// e.g. prefixed("s", "a, b") -> "s.a, s.b". Used to disambiguate the sessions columns
875	// in the FTS join (where session_id/agent also exist on the FTS table).
876	func prefixed(alias, cols string) string {
877		parts := strings.Split(cols, ",")
878		for i, p := range parts {
879			parts[i] = alias + "." + strings.TrimSpace(p)
880		}
881		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
882	}
883	
884	// scanSessions scans rows selected with sessionColumns (in order) into Sessions.
885	func scanSessions(rows *sql.Rows) ([]Session, error) {
886		var out []Session
887		for rows.Next() {
888			var s Session
889			if err := rows.Scan(
890				&s.ProjectID, &s.ProjectName, &s.Agent, &s.SessionID, &s.CreatedAt, &s.UpdatedAt,
891				&s.UserTurns, &s.TotalTurns, &s.Slug, &s.Name, &s.NativePath, &s.OriginCwd,
892				&s.Size, &s.Mtime, &s.IndexVersion, &s.IndexedAt,
893			); err != nil {
894				return nil, err
895			}
896			out = append(out, s)
897		}
898		return out, rows.Err()
899	}
900

224	// FetchSessionData streams a session's SessionData blob and returns the raw JSON bytes.
225	// It does NOT unmarshal into schema.SessionData — the resume layer does that (and checks
226	// schemaVersion), keeping this package decoupled from the schema package, exactly as the sync
227	// push treats SessionData as an opaque string. Uses a custom request (not skillsAPIRequest)
228	// because it needs the SessionData Accept header and a raw-bytes body, not JSON decoding.
229	func FetchSessionData(projectID, sessionID string) ([]byte, error) {
230		apiURL := GetAPIBaseURL() + "/api/v1/projects/" +
231			url.PathEscape(projectID) + "/sessions/" + url.PathEscape(sessionID)
232	
233		req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, apiURL, nil)
234		if err != nil {
235			return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating session-data request: %w", err)
236		}
237		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+GetCloudToken())
238		req.Header.Set("Accept", sessionDataMediaType)
239		req.Header.Set("User-Agent", GetUserAgent())
240	
241		client := &http.Client{Timeout: cloudResumeHTTPTimeout}
242		resp, err := client.Do(req)
243		if err != nil {
244			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch session data failed: %w", err)
245		}
246		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
247	
248		body, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
249		if err != nil {
250			return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading session data response: %w", err)
251		}
252	
253		switch {
254		case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized:
255			return nil, &ErrAuthenticationFailed{Message: "not authenticated to SpecStory Cloud"}
256		case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden:
257			// The requireFeature("resume") gate — the user isn't on a qualifying plan.
258			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro")
259		case resp.StatusCode == http.StatusNotFound:
260			return nil, fmt.Errorf("session data not found in cloud")
261		case resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300:
262			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetch session data returned status %d", resp.StatusCode)
263		}
264	
265		return body, nil
266	}

136		searchCancel context.CancelFunc

138		// previewing shows a glamour-rendered, scrollable reader for the highlighted session,
139		// identical to search's reader (see openPreview / renderPreview).
140		previewing    bool
141		reader        viewport.Model
142		readerSession *sessionindex.Session
143		// previewSeq is bumped on every openPreview. A cloud preview loads its markdown off-thread
144		// (a blob fetch), so its late-arriving result is applied only when this seq still matches —
145		// dropping the result if the user has since closed the reader or moved to another session.
146		previewSeq int
147	
148		// confirmingDelete is a top-level modal (like previewing): 'd' in a session list, the global
149		// search results, or the project browser opens a y/N soft-delete confirmation for pendingDelete.
150		confirmingDelete bool
151		pendingDelete    pendingDelete
152	
153		// statusMsg is a transient one-line notice (currently only a failed delete) shown under the
154		// footer until the next keypress. A soft delete otherwise gives no feedback beyond the row
155		// disappearing, so a failure would look like a silent no-op without this.
156		statusMsg string
157	
158		// Cloud resume: SpecStory Cloud sessions from the user's OTHER machines, blended
159		// into the browser best-effort and local-first. Eligibility (logged-in + Pro) is
160		// checked once, async, off the UI thread; cloudEligible gates fetches; cloudPending drives the
161		// "searching cloud…" indicator; cloudNudge is the footer invitation shown to ineligible users.
162		// agentIDByName reverse-maps a cloud row's display agent name ("Claude Code") back to
163		// the provider id ("claude") that dedup and the resume/reconstruct path key on.
164		cloudChecked  bool
165		cloudEligible bool
166		cloudPending  bool
167		cloudNudge    string
168		// cloudAll holds the active project's cloud sessions SEPARATELY from m.all. They must not live
169		// in m.all: the background index warm and post-delete refresh both do `m.all = ListByProject()`,
170		// which would discard anything merged into it. Instead they're merged with m.all at filter time
171		// (refilterCurrentAgent), so a local re-query can't wipe them.
172		cloudAll      []sessionindex.Session
173		cloudProjects []cloud.CloudProject // cloud projects, each carrying its resumable session summaries inline; merged into the browser at filter time
174		// cloudLocalKeys is the local per-project session fingerprint set, fetched alongside
175		// cloudProjects so the all-projects rollup can dedup cloud sessions against local by
176		// (agent, session_id) — local preferred — and recompute accurate per-agent chips / totals / last
177		// activity from the union. Nil until the first cloud-projects fetch completes.
178		cloudLocalKeys map[string][]sessionindex.ProjectSessionKey
179		agentIDByName  map[string]string // agent display name -> provider id
180	
181		// Machine filter (the `m` key), modeled on the agent filter: cycle all → "local only" → each
182		// remote machine. Only meaningful once cloud rows from OTHER machines are present, so the ring
183		// is just [all] until then. Keyed by stable deviceId; displayed by machineName.
184		machineFilter string         // "" = all; "local" = this machine; else a remote deviceId
185		machineCycle  []machineEntry // the filter ring, rebuilt from cloud rows in play
186		deviceID      string         // this machine's stable id (for the "local only" match)
187	
188		// Cloud search (global search view). Kept separate from the local FTS results, exactly like
189		// cloudAll vs all in browse, so a fresh local query (per keystroke) and a cloud result (on the
190		// slower fire-on-pause debounce) don't clobber each other; rebuildGlobalResults merges them.
191		globalLocal         []sessionindex.Session // raw local FTS results for the active global query
192		globalCloud         []sessionindex.Session // cloud search hits for the active global query
193		globalCloudSnippets map[string]string      // cloud snippets, keyed by FingerprintKey(agent, id)
194		cloudSearchSeq      int                    // debounce seq for cloud search (separate from searchSeq)
195		cloudSearchPending  bool                   // a cloud search is in flight (drives the indicator)
196	
197		// Cloud search for the project-scoped list search (`/` inside a drilled-in project). Same
198		// separate-slice pattern as globalCloud: the server scopes these to the active project, and
199		// refilterCurrentAgent merges them into m.filtered so a per-keystroke local re-query can't
200		// discard them.
201		listCloud         []sessionindex.Session
202		listCloudSnippets map[string]string // cloud snippets for the list search, keyed by FingerprintKey
203	
204		mode         tuiMode
205		chosen       *sessionindex.Session
206		targetCursor int
207	
208		width, height int
209		result        sessionTUIResult
210	}
211	
212	// sessionTUIOpts carries the per-command entry configuration. The only real differences
213	// between `resume` and `search` live here: the header title, what the positional arg means
214	// (presetTo vs. initialQuery), and whether to open in the all-projects search.
215	type sessionTUIOpts struct {
216		title         string // header title ("SpecStory Resume" / "SpecStory Search")
217		presetTo      string // resume: pre-selected target agent (from `resume <agent>`)
218		lastAgent     string // default target (last resumed), or ""
219		viewMode      string // "dense" | "sparse"
220		initialQuery  string // search: pre-seed the all-projects query
221		startInSearch bool   // search: open in the all-projects FTS with the input focused
222	}
223	
224	func newSessionTUI(store *sessionindex.Store, registry *factory.Registry, projectID, projectName string,
225		sessions []sessionindex.Session, agents map[string]agentMeta, installed []agentChoice, opts sessionTUIOpts) sessionTUI {
226	
227		ti := textinput.New()
228		ti.Prompt = "/ "
229		pi := textinput.New()
230		pi.Prompt = "p "
231		gi := textinput.New()
232		gi.Prompt = "/ "
233	
234		m := sessionTUI{
235			store:           store,
236			registry:        registry,
237			title:           opts.title,
238			reader:          viewport.New(),
239			projectID:       projectID,
240			projectName:     projectName,
241			homeProjectID:   projectID,
242			homeProjectName: projectName,
243			homeSessions:    sessions,
244			agents:          agents,
245			installed:       installed,
246			presetTo:        opts.presetTo,
247			lastAgent:       opts.lastAgent,
248			all:             sessions,
249			viewMode:        opts.viewMode,
250			search:          ti,
251			projSearch:      pi,
252			globalInput:     gi,
253		}
254		// Reverse map for blending cloud rows: their metadata carries the display agent name, but
255		// dedup and resume key on the provider id.
256		m.agentIDByName = make(map[string]string, len(agents))
257		for id, meta := range agents {
258			m.agentIDByName[meta.name] = id
259		}
260		m.deviceID = cloud.DeviceID()
261		m.rebuildAgentCycle()
262		m.applyFilter()
263	
264		switch {
265		case opts.startInSearch:
266			// `search`: land directly in the all-projects FTS, input focused (so the user types
267			// immediately, exactly like before). Init fires the pre-seeded query, if any. The
268			// search IS the root view here, so esc quits rather than unwinding into the browser.
269			m.startedInSearch = true
270			m.enterBrowser()
271			m.globalActive = true
272			m.globalSearching = true
273			m.globalQuery = opts.initialQuery
274			m.globalInput.SetValue(opts.initialQuery)
275			m.globalInput.Focus() // focus state persists on the stored model; Init returns the blink+query cmds
276			if queryReady(m.globalQuery) {
277				m.searchSeq = 1
278			}
279		case len(sessions) == 0:
280			// `resume` with an empty current project → open straight into the all-projects browser.
281			m.startedInBrowser = true
282			m.enterBrowser()
283		}
284		return m
285	}
286	
287	func (m sessionTUI) Init() tea.Cmd {
288		// Kick the async cloud-eligibility check once on open (off the UI thread). When it resolves,
289		// Update either starts the first cloud fetch (eligible) or sets the footer nudge.
290		cmds := []tea.Cmd{cloudEligibilityCmd()}
291		// Search starts focused in the all-projects input; kick the blink and any pre-seeded query.
292		if m.globalSearching {
293			cmds = append(cmds, m.globalInput.Focus())
294			if queryReady(m.globalQuery) {
295				cmds = append(cmds, searchDebounce(m.searchSeq, modeProjects))
296			}
297		}
298		return tea.Batch(cmds...)
299	}
300	
301	func (m sessionTUI) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
302		switch msg := msg.(type) {
303		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
304			m.width, m.height = msg.Width, msg.Height
305			m.reader.SetWidth(m.width)
306			m.reader.SetHeight(m.previewHeight())
307			return m, nil
308		case indexWarmedMsg:
309			return m.refreshAfterWarm()
310		case searchDebounceMsg:
311			// Fire the actual query only if no newer keystroke has arrived (debounce).
312			if msg.seq == m.searchSeq {
313				if m.searchCancel != nil {
314					m.searchCancel() // abort any prior in-flight query, freeing its connection
315				}
316				ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
317				m.searchCancel = cancel
318				return m, m.runSearch(msg.seq, msg.kind, ctx)
319			}
320			return m, nil
321		case searchResultMsg:
322			// Apply only the latest query's results (discard stale async results).
323			if msg.seq == m.searchSeq {
324				m.applySearchResults(msg.kind, msg.sessions)
325				return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(msg.kind)
326			}
327			return m, nil
328		case snippetResultMsg:
329			if msg.seq == m.snippetSeq {
330				if msg.kind == modeProjects {
331					if m.globalSnippets == nil {
332						m.globalSnippets = map[string]string{}
333					}
334					for key, snip := range msg.snippets {
335						m.globalSnippets[key] = snip
336					}
337				} else {
338					if m.filteredSnippets == nil {
339						m.filteredSnippets = map[string]string{}
340					}
341					for key, snip := range msg.snippets {
342						m.filteredSnippets[key] = snip
343					}
344				}
345			}
346			return m, nil
347		case cloudEligibilityMsg:
348			return m.applyCloudEligibility(msg)
349		case cloudSessionsMsg:
350			return m.applyCloudSessions(msg)
351		case cloudProjectsMsg:
352			return m.applyCloudProjects(msg)
353		case cloudDeleteResultMsg:
354			return m.applyCloudDeleteResult(msg)
355		case cloudSearchDebounceMsg:
356			return m.applyCloudSearchDebounce(msg)
357		case cloudSearchResultMsg:
358			return m.applyCloudSearchResult(msg)
359		case cloudPreviewMsg:
360			return m.applyCloudPreview(msg)
361		case tea.KeyPressMsg:
362			// Any keypress dismisses a lingering status notice (e.g. a failed delete); it has served
363			// its purpose once the user has read it and moved on.
364			m.statusMsg = ""
365			switch {
366			case m.confirmingDelete:
367				// The delete confirmation is a top-level modal, reachable from the list, the global
368				// results, or the project browser, so it is checked before any mode-specific routing.
369				return m.updateDeleteConfirm(msg)
370			case m.previewing:
371				// The preview is a top-level overlay: it opens over the list OR the global
372				// results, so it must be checked before any mode-specific routing.
373				return m.updatePreview(msg)
374			case m.mode == modeTarget:
375				return m.updateTarget(msg)
376			case m.mode == modeProjects:
377				switch {
378				case m.globalSearching:
379					return m.updateGlobalSearch(msg)
380				case m.globalActive:
381					return m.updateGlobalResults(msg)
382				case m.projSearching:
383					return m.updateProjectSearch(msg)
384				default:
385					return m.updateProjects(msg)
386				}
387			case m.searching:
388				return m.updateSearch(msg)
389			default:
390				return m.updateList(msg)
391			}
392		}
393		return m, nil
394	}
395	
396	// refreshAfterWarm re-queries the index after the background current-project warm pass lands,
397	// so newly created or changed sessions for THIS project appear without a restart. It refreshes
398	// in place only when the home project's session list is what's on screen (preserving the
399	// cursor by session id), or re-runs a settled cross-project search to fold in the fresh rows.
400	// In any other view it just caches the refreshed sessions for when the user returns home.
401	func (m sessionTUI) refreshAfterWarm() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
402		sessions, err := m.store.ListByProject(m.homeProjectID)
403		if err != nil {
404			slog.Debug("resume: refresh after warm failed", "error", err)
405			return m, nil
406		}
407		m.homeSessions = sessions
408	
409		// In-place refresh when the home project's list is the active view.
410		if m.mode == modeList && !m.inBrowser && m.projectID == m.homeProjectID {
411			selID := ""
412			if sel := m.selected(); sel != nil {
413				selID = sel.SessionID
414			}
415			m.all = sessions
416			m.rebuildAgentCycle()
417			m.applyFilter()
418			m.cursor = indexOfSession(m.filtered, selID)
419			m.clampScroll()
420			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
421		}
422	
423		// A settled cross-project search (not mid-typing): re-run it so refreshed rows show up.
424		// While typing, the user's own debounced queries already see the fresh data.
425		if m.mode == modeProjects && m.globalActive && !m.globalSearching && queryReady(m.globalQuery) {
426			m.searchSeq++
427			return m, searchDebounce(m.searchSeq, modeProjects)
428		}
429		return m, nil
430	}
431	
432	// indexOfSession returns the position of the session with id in list, or 0 when not present
433	// (so a refreshed list with a deleted selection lands safely at the top).
434	func indexOfSession(list []sessionindex.Session, id string) int {
435		if id == "" {
436			return 0
437		}
438		for i := range list {
439			if list[i].SessionID == id {
440				return i
441			}
442		}
443		return 0
444	}
445	
446	// updateList handles keys while browsing the session list.
447	func (m sessionTUI) updateList(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
448		switch msg.String() {
449		case "q", "ctrl+c":
450			m.result = sessionTUIResult{cancelled: true}
451			return m, tea.Quit
452		case "esc":
453			// In a drilled-in project, esc returns to the browser; at home it quits.
454			if m.inBrowser {
455				m.enterBrowser()
456				return m, nil
457			}
458			m.result = sessionTUIResult{cancelled: true}
459			return m, tea.Quit
460		case "tab":
461			// Toggle scope: home list ↔ all-projects browser.
462			m.enterBrowser()
463			return m, nil
464		case "up", "k":
465			m.moveCursor(-1)
466			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
467		case "down", "j":
468			m.moveCursor(1)
469			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
470		case "pgup":
471			m.moveCursor(-m.listHeight())
472			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
473		case "pgdown":
474			m.moveCursor(m.listHeight())
475			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
476		case "home", "g":
477			m.cursor, m.top = 0, 0
478			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
479		case "end", "G":
480			m.cursor = len(m.filtered) - 1
481			m.clampScroll()
482			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
483		case "r":
484			// Resume the highlighted session. Enter is NOT a resume trigger (a stray return
485			// shouldn't launch an agent); it previews, aliased to space below.
486			if sel := m.selected(); sel != nil {
487				return m.beginResume(sel)
488			}
489		// Enter is silently aliased to space so either key previews (the hint only advertises
490		// space). 'r' remains the sole resume trigger.
491		case " ", "space", "enter":
492			if sel := m.selected(); sel != nil {
493				return m.openPreview(sel)
494			}
495		case "/":
496			m.searching = true
497			m.search.SetValue(m.searchQuery)
498			return m, m.search.Focus()
499		case "a":
500			return m, m.cycleAgent()
501		case "m":
502			return m, m.cycleMachine()
503		case "v":
504			m.toggleViewMode()
505			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
506		case "u":
507			if cmd := m.upgradeCmd(); cmd != nil {
508				return m, cmd
509			}
510		case "d":
511			if sel := m.selected(); sel != nil {
512				m.pendingDelete = pendingDelete{source: deleteFromList, agent: sel.Agent, sessionID: sel.SessionID, projectID: sel.ProjectID, isCloud: sel.IsCloud, label: sessionTitle(*sel)}
513				m.confirmingDelete = true
514			}
515		}
516		return m, nil
517	}
518	
519	// updateDeleteConfirm handles the y/N soft-delete confirmation modal. Deletion requires an
520	// explicit "y"; every other key (n, esc, q, or a stray press) cancels, so the destructive path
521	// is never the default.
522	func (m sessionTUI) updateDeleteConfirm(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
523		switch msg.String() {
524		case "y", "Y":
525			return m.performDelete()
526		case "ctrl+c":
527			m.result = sessionTUIResult{cancelled: true}
528			return m, tea.Quit
529		default:
530			m.confirmingDelete = false
531		}
532		return m, nil
533	}
534	
535	// performDelete applies the pending soft delete, records an analytics event, and refreshes the
536	// originating view. A soft delete hides the session(s) from the picker/search and stops reindex
537	// re-adding them; the native session files on disk are left untouched.
538	func (m sessionTUI) performDelete() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
539		m.confirmingDelete = false
540		pd := m.pendingDelete
541	
542		// Cloud rows delete from SpecStory Cloud via the API, async so a slow/down server can't freeze
543		// the TUI. The row stays until the delete confirms (applyCloudDeleteResult removes it).
544		if pd.isCloud {
545			return m, cloudDeleteCmd(pd)
546		}
547	
548		affected, err := softDeletePending(pd)
549		if err != nil {
550			slog.Debug("resume: soft delete failed", "error", err)
551			m.statusMsg = "Delete failed — " + pd.label + " left in place"
552			return m, nil
553		}
554	
555		scope := "session"
556		if pd.source == deleteFromProjects {
557			scope = "project"
558		}
559		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSessionDeleted, analytics.Properties{
560			"scope":    scope,
561			"agent":    pd.agent,
562			"affected": affected,
563		})
564	
565		return m.refreshAfterDelete(pd)
566	}
567	
568	// softDeletePending opens a short-lived writer handle to sessions.db — the browse handle is
569	// read-only (OpenReader) — applies the tombstone, and closes it. Delete is a rare interactive
570	// action, so the open/close cost is irrelevant; WAL lets this writer commit alongside the read
571	// handle and the background warm's writer.
572	func softDeletePending(pd pendingDelete) (int, error) {
573		dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
574		if err != nil {
575			return 0, err
576		}
577		w, err := sessionindex.Open(dbPath)
578		if err != nil {
579			return 0, err
580		}
581		defer func() { _ = w.Close() }()
582	
583		if pd.source == deleteFromProjects {
584			return w.SoftDeleteProject(pd.projectID)
585		}
586		return w.SoftDeleteSession(pd.agent, pd.sessionID)
587	}
588	
589	// refreshAfterDelete re-syncs the view the delete was triggered from so the removed session or
590	// project drops out immediately, without a restart. The read handle (m.store) sees the writer's
591	// committed change on its next query (WAL starts a fresh read snapshot per statement).
592	func (m sessionTUI) refreshAfterDelete(pd pendingDelete) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
593		switch pd.source {
594		case deleteFromProjects:
595			// Re-roll the project list; a project with no live sessions left drops out entirely.
596			m.projectsLoaded = false
597			m.enterBrowser()
598			// Deleting the last project would leave the cursor past the shortened list, so clamp it
599			// (mirrors the session-list and global paths below) before fixing the scroll window.
600			m.projCursor = clampIndex(m.projCursor, len(m.projFiltered))
601			m.clampProjScroll()
602			return m, nil
603		case deleteFromGlobal:
604			// Drop the deleted hit from the in-memory results. Its FTS row is already gone, so a
605			// re-query would also exclude it, but removing in place avoids an async round trip.
606			m.globalResults = removeSession(m.globalResults, pd.agent, pd.sessionID)
607			delete(m.globalSnippets, sessionindex.FingerprintKey(pd.agent, pd.sessionID))
608			m.globalCursor = clampIndex(m.globalCursor, len(m.globalResults))
609			m.clampGlobalScroll()
610			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeProjects)
611		default: // deleteFromList
612			// Re-query the active project (home or drilled-in) and rebuild. The cursor keeps its
613			// index (clamped), so the next session slides up under it.
614			sessions, err := m.store.ListByProject(m.projectID)
615			if err != nil {
616				slog.Debug("resume: refresh after delete failed", "error", err)
617				return m, nil
618			}
619			if m.projectID == m.homeProjectID {
620				m.homeSessions = sessions
621			}
622			m.all = sessions
623			m.rebuildAgentCycle()
624			m.applyFilter()
625			m.cursor = clampIndex(m.cursor, len(m.filtered))
626			m.clampScroll()
627			return m, m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
628		}
629	}
630	
631	// removeSession returns sessions without the (agent, sessionID) entry.
632	func removeSession(sessions []sessionindex.Session, agent, sessionID string) []sessionindex.Session {
633		out := make([]sessionindex.Session, 0, len(sessions))
634		for _, s := range sessions {
635			if s.Agent == agent && s.SessionID == sessionID {
636				continue
637			}
638			out = append(out, s)
639		}
640		return out
641	}
642	
643	// clampIndex keeps a cursor within [0, n-1], or 0 when the list is empty.
644	func clampIndex(i, n int) int {
645		if i > n-1 {
646			i = n - 1
647		}
648		if i < 0 {
649			i = 0
650		}
651		return i
652	}
653	
654	// updateSearch handles the full-text search input. The typed character is applied to the
655	// input immediately (instant feedback); the FTS query runs async + debounced so a slow
656	// query never blocks typing. See searchDebounceMsg / searchResultMsg.
657	func (m sessionTUI) updateSearch(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
658		switch msg.String() {
659		case "esc":
660			m.searching = false
661			m.search.Blur()
662			m.searchQuery = ""
663			m.searchSeq++ // invalidate any in-flight search
664			m.cloudSearchSeq++
665			m.listCloud = nil
666			m.listCloudSnippets = nil
667			m.snippetSeq++
668			m.applyFilter()
669			return m, nil
670		case "enter":
671			m.searching = false
672			m.search.Blur()
673			return m, nil
674		case "up", "down", "pgup", "pgdown":
675			// Arrows do nothing inside the one-line input, so commit the search and let the same
676			// key move the now-focused list — the user reaches a result without a separate enter.
677			m.searching = false
678			m.search.Blur()
679			return m.updateList(msg)
680		}
681		var cmd tea.Cmd
682		m.search, cmd = m.search.Update(msg)
683		m.searchQuery = m.search.Value()
684		m.searchSeq++
685		m.cloudSearchSeq++ // supersede any in-flight cloud search
686		// Current cloud hits are for the previous query — drop them so a fresh local result doesn't merge
687		// stale cloud rows; the fire-on-pause cloud search refills them.
688		m.listCloud = nil
689		m.listCloudSnippets = nil
690		if !queryReady(m.searchQuery) {
691			// Too short to search: show the full (agent-filtered) list synchronously.
692			m.cloudSearchPending = false
693			m.snippetSeq++
694			m.applyFilter()
695			return m, cmd
696		}

705	// updatePreview handles keys while the glamour preview reader is open. Close keys return to
706	// the underlying screen (list or global results); `r` resumes the previewed session;
707	// everything else (↑↓ pgup/pgdn) scrolls the viewport.
708	func (m sessionTUI) updatePreview(msg tea.KeyPressMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
709		switch msg.String() {

714		case "r":

784	// ---- list mechanics ----
785	
786	// moveCursorWithin advances *cursor by delta within a list of n items, clamping to
787	// [0, n-1] and then realigning the scroll window via clampScrollWithin. It is the
788	// shared core of the three list cursors (sessions, projects, global search), which
789	// differ only in which fields they track. A no-op for an empty list.
790	func moveCursorWithin(cursor, top *int, delta, n, height int) {
791		if n == 0 {
792			return
793		}
794		*cursor += delta
795		if *cursor < 0 {
796			*cursor = 0
797		}
798		if *cursor > n-1 {
799			*cursor = n - 1
800		}
801		clampScrollWithin(cursor, top, height)
802	}
803	
804	// clampScrollWithin keeps the scroll window [*top, *top+height) covering *cursor.
805	func clampScrollWithin(cursor, top *int, height int) {
806		if *cursor < *top {
807			*top = *cursor
808		}
809		if *cursor >= *top+height {
810			*top = *cursor - height + 1
811		}
812		if *top < 0 {
813			*top = 0
814		}
815	}

817	func (m *sessionTUI) moveCursor(delta int) {

823	}

854	func (m *sessionTUI) rebuildAgentCycle() {
855		present := map[string]bool{}
856		for _, s := range m.all {
857			present[s.Agent] = true
858		}
859		// Cloud rows can introduce agents not present locally, so include them in the filter ring.
860		for _, s := range m.cloudAll {
861			present[s.Agent] = true
862		}
863		ids := make([]string, 0, len(present))
864		for id := range present {
865			ids = append(ids, id)
866		}
867		sort.Strings(ids)
868		m.agentCycle = append([]string{""}, ids...)
869		// The machine ring is derived from the same row set (specifically the cloud rows), so keep it
870		// in lockstep with the agent ring.
871		m.rebuildMachineCycle()

874	func (m *sessionTUI) cycleAgent() tea.Cmd {
875		// In the all-projects search, cycle over every known agent and re-run the query; in a
876		// session list, cycle over the agents actually present and re-filter in place.
877		if m.mode == modeProjects && m.globalActive {
878			m.agentFilter = nextInCycle(m.allAgentCycle(), m.agentFilter)
879			m.searchSeq++
880			return searchDebounce(m.searchSeq, modeProjects)
881		}
882		m.agentFilter = nextInCycle(m.agentCycle, m.agentFilter)
883		// Re-filter the cached results in memory — the agent filter is client-side, so cycling it
884		// must not trigger applyFilter's synchronous FTS query on the UI thread.
885		m.refilterCurrentAgent()
886		return m.requestVisibleSnippets(modeList)
887	}

889	// allAgentCycle is the agent-filter ring for cross-project search: "" then every known agent.
890	func (m sessionTUI) allAgentCycle() []string {
891		ids := make([]string, 0, len(m.agents))
892		for id := range m.agents {
893			ids = append(ids, id)
894		}
895		sort.Strings(ids)
896		return append([]string{""}, ids...)
897	}

899	// nextInCycle returns the element after cur in cycle, wrapping around.
900	func nextInCycle(cycle []string, cur string) string {
901		idx := 0
902		for i, id := range cycle {
903			if id == cur {
904				idx = i
905				break
906			}
907		}
908		return cycle[(idx+1)%len(cycle)]
909	}

911	func (m *sessionTUI) toggleViewMode() {
912		if m.viewMode == "sparse" {
913			m.viewMode = "dense"
914		} else {
915			m.viewMode = "sparse"
916		}
917		m.clampScroll()
918	}

920	// applyFilter rebuilds the visible list from the agent filter and search query. When a search
921	// is active it runs the FTS query, caches the raw results (searchRaw), then applies the agent
922	// filter; otherwise the list is the project's sessions filtered by agent. Snippets are fetched
923	// lazily for the visible rows. Callers that only change the agent filter should use
924	// refilterCurrentAgent, which reuses searchRaw and avoids a second query.
925	func (m *sessionTUI) applyFilter() {
926		if queryReady(m.searchQuery) {
927			m.searchRaw, _ = m.store.Search(ftsQuery(m.searchQuery), m.projectID)
928		} else {
929			m.searchRaw = nil
930		}
931		m.refilterCurrentAgent()
932	}
933	
934	// refilterCurrentAgent re-derives the visible list for the current agent filter WITHOUT a new
935	// FTS query. The agent filter is applied client-side, so cycling agents during a search only
936	// needs to re-filter the cached raw results (searchRaw) — keeping `a` off the synchronous DB
937	// path that applyFilter would otherwise take on every keystroke. With no active search it
938	// filters the project's sessions (m.all).
939	func (m *sessionTUI) refilterCurrentAgent() {
940		searching := queryReady(m.searchQuery)
941		src := m.all
942		// Browse (no active search): blend the active project's cloud sessions with the local ones —
943		// deduped local-preferred and re-sorted by recency. Kept out of m.all so local re-queries
944		// (index warm, post-delete refresh) can't discard them. Search stays local-only for now.
945		if len(m.cloudAll) > 0 {
946			src = mergeCloudRows(m.all, m.cloudAll)
947		}
948		if searching {
949			// Blend the project's cloud search hits (fetched server-side, scoped to this project) with the
950			// local FTS results — deduped local-preferred and recency-sorted, the same merge browse and
951			// global search use. Kept out of searchRaw so a per-keystroke local re-query can't drop them.
952			src = m.searchRaw
953			if len(m.listCloud) > 0 {
954				src = mergeCloudRows(m.searchRaw, m.listCloud)
955			}
956		}
957		out := make([]sessionindex.Session, 0, len(src))
958		for _, s := range src {
959			if m.agentFilter != "" && s.Agent != m.agentFilter {
960				continue
961			}
962			if !m.machineMatch(s) {
963				continue
964			}
965			out = append(out, s)
966		}
967		m.filtered = out
968		if searching {
969			// Keep any snippets already fetched (keyed by agent/session, so still valid); ensure the
970			// map exists so requestVisibleSnippets can fill in the now-visible rows.
971			if m.filteredSnippets == nil {
972				m.filteredSnippets = map[string]string{}
973			}
974		} else {
975			m.filteredSnippets = nil
976		}
977	
978		if m.cursor > len(m.filtered)-1 {
979			m.cursor = len(m.filtered) - 1
980		}
981		if m.cursor < 0 {
982			m.cursor = 0
983		}
984		m.top = 0
985		m.clampScroll()
986	}
987	
988	// beginResume advances from a chosen session toward launch. When a target agent was
989	// pre-selected via `resume <agent>`, that choice is honored immediately and the picker exits
990	// — the user is never asked to pick a target. Otherwise it moves to the target-selection step.
991	func (m sessionTUI) beginResume(sess *sessionindex.Session) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
992		m.chosen = sess
993		if m.presetTo != "" {
994			m.result = sessionTUIResult{session: sess, targetID: m.presetTo}
995			return m, tea.Quit
996		}
997		m.mode = modeTarget
998		m.targetCursor = m.defaultTargetIndex()
999		return m, nil
1000	}
1001	
1002	func (m sessionTUI) defaultTargetIndex() int {
1003		// Prefer the last-resumed agent, else the chosen session's own agent (same-agent resume).
1004		// An explicit preset (`resume <agent>`) never reaches here — beginResume skips the
1005		// target-selection step entirely in that case.
1006		want := m.lastAgent
1007		if want == "" && m.chosen != nil {
1008			want = m.chosen.Agent
1009		}
1010		for i, a := range m.installed {
1011			if a.id == want {
1012				return i
1013			}
1014		}
1015		return 0
1016	}

19	// machineEntry is one stop in the machine-filter ring: a stable key and its display label.
20	type machineEntry struct {
21		key   string // "" (all machines), "local" (this machine), or a remote deviceId
22		label string // "all machines", "local only", or a machineName (disambiguated if it collides)
23	}

25	// rebuildMachineCycle derives the machine-filter ring from the current cloud rows. The ring is
26	// [all] until cloud rows from OTHER machines exist, at which point it becomes all → "local only" →
27	// each remote machine (keyed by stable deviceId, labelled by machineName, sorted by deviceId for
28	// stable order; duplicate names get (1)/(2) suffixes). This machine never appears as its own remote
29	// entry — it's covered by "local only".
30	func (m *sessionTUI) rebuildMachineCycle() {
31		// Latest machineName per remote deviceId, across whichever cloud rows are in play (browse's
32		// cloudAll and search's globalCloud).
33		names := map[string]string{}
34		addMachine := func(rows []sessionindex.Session) {
35			for _, s := range rows {
36				if !s.IsCloud || s.DeviceID == "" || s.DeviceID == m.deviceID {
37					continue
38				}
39				if s.MachineName != "" {
40					names[s.DeviceID] = s.MachineName
41				} else if _, ok := names[s.DeviceID]; !ok {
42					names[s.DeviceID] = shortID(s.DeviceID)
43				}
44			}
45		}
46		addMachine(m.cloudAll)
47		addMachine(m.globalCloud)
48	
49		if len(names) == 0 {
50			// No other machines to distinguish — the filter would be a no-op, so hide it.
51			m.machineCycle = []machineEntry{{key: "", label: "all machines"}}
52			m.machineFilter = ""
53			return
54		}
55	
56		ids := make([]string, 0, len(names))
57		for id := range names {
58			ids = append(ids, id)
59		}
60		sort.Strings(ids)
61	
62		// Disambiguate duplicate machine names with deterministic (1)/(2) suffixes.
63		labelCount := map[string]int{}
64		for _, id := range ids {
65			labelCount[names[id]]++
66		}
67		labelSeen := map[string]int{}
68	
69		cycle := []machineEntry{{key: "", label: "all machines"}, {key: "local", label: "local only"}}
70		for _, id := range ids {
71			label := names[id]
72			if labelCount[label] > 1 {
73				labelSeen[label]++
74				label = fmt.Sprintf("%s (%d)", label, labelSeen[label])
75			}
76			cycle = append(cycle, machineEntry{key: id, label: label})
77		}
78		m.machineCycle = cycle
79	
80		// If the active filter's machine dropped out of the ring, fall back to all.
81		if !machineKeyInCycle(cycle, m.machineFilter) {
82			m.machineFilter = ""
83		}
84	}
