224	+
225	+Two facts make this cheap. First, the web permalink (`https://cloud-dev.specstory.com/projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}`) already carries exactly the two IDs the cloud API needs: `projectId` is the CLI-minted truncated-SHA `project_id` (the same value in local `sessions.db` and in `workspaces.project_id`), and `sessionId` is the native session UUID (= local `session_id` = cloud `client_id`) — precisely the arguments of `cloud.FetchSessionData(projectID, sessionID)` (`resume_client.go:229`). Second, the TUI already has the seam: the target-picker step (`modeTarget`) operates on a pinned `chosen` session (`session_tui.go:993-998`), so a URI-resolved session can enter the picker at the target step — or bypass the TUI entirely when `[agent]` is given. **No server changes** — every endpoint this chunk needs shipped in Chunks 1–4.
226	+
227	+- **D28 — `--session <uri>` is non-interactive session *selection* on the TUI's code path.** The flag resolves the URI to the same session identity the picker would produce (including D13's local-preferred selection-time guard) and feeds the identical `resumePlan` → `launchResume` machinery (`resume.go:216`) — no parallel resume implementation. Registered on `resume` only, in `CreateResumeCommand` (`resume.go:70`), **not** in `registerResumeLaunchFlags` (`resume.go:154`, shared with `search`).
228	+- **D29 — Three accepted URI forms, one parser.** (1) **Custom scheme** `specstory://projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID}` — the **canonical form and what the web app's resume dialog copies (D36)**: host-free (no D30 host question by construction) and it reserves the door for a future OS protocol handler. (Parser note: `url.Parse` puts `projects` in `Host` for a custom scheme — rejoin host+path before matching.) (2) **Web permalink** `https://{host}/projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID}` — accepted so a user can paste their browser URL bar directly; same path grammar; trailing slashes tolerated (matching the existing cloud-URL normalization) and path segments after the session id (e.g. `/chats/{chatId}`) ignored, so any session-page URL pastes cleanly. (3) **Bare session UUID** — shorthand, resolves local-first then cloud. ID shapes are validated up front for early, clear errors: project id is the `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx` 16-hex-char form (`createHash`, `pkg/utils/project_identity.go:256`), session id is a UUID; both case-insensitive.
229	+- **D30 — A pasted URL contributes IDs only; the Bearer token only ever goes to the *configured* cloud URL.** The CLI never adopts the permalink's host. If the permalink's host differs from the configured cloud host (default `https://cloud.specstory.com`, overridable via `--cloud-url`/config), fail with: "This link points at {host}, but the CLI is configured for {configured}. Pass --cloud-url https://{host} if this is intentional." Rationale: a crafted "resume link" must not exfiltrate the user's token to an attacker's host. Bare-UUID and `specstory://` forms carry no host, so no check applies.
230	+- **D31 — Resolution order mirrors TUI selection.** (1) **Local index first**: look up the session id across agents in `sessions.db` (`deleted = 0`; a new store query — `GetSession`, `store.go:639`, is `(agent, session_id)`-keyed and can't do this) — found means a local in-place resume using the row's `agent`/`origin_cwd`, exactly like D13's guard (this also makes a pasted *cloud* permalink resume locally, offline-capable, when the session exists here). In the near-impossible event two agents share a session UUID, prefer the most recent `updated_at`. (2) **Else cloud**, gated by D10 eligibility surfaced as actionable errors instead of nudges (not logged in → "Log into SpecStory Cloud (specstory login) to resume sessions from your other machines."; 403 → the existing "requires SpecStory Pro" mapping in `FetchSessionData`): with a project id in hand, fetch directly; a bare UUID checks the current project's cloud list (`ListCloudSessions`) then the all-projects `?resumable=true` listing (D24 embeds every resumable session, one request) to discover the owning project. (3) **Else** a "session not found" error naming where it looked. D12's `schemaVersion` guard and cross-project resume semantics are inherited unchanged from the shared path.
231	+- **D32 — The `[agent]` positional stays the target override; omitting it opens the TUI directly at the target picker.** `resume <agent> --session <uri>` is fully non-interactive (plan built directly, no TUI — the `presetTo` short-circuit's equivalent). `resume --session <uri>` launches the TUI in `modeTarget` with the resolved session pinned as `chosen`, default highlight logic unchanged (last-resumed agent, else the session's own agent — `defaultTargetIndex`, `session_tui.go:1002`). Consequence: the web-copied command omits the agent — the terminal owns target choice, so the web dialog needs **no** provider picker.
232	+- **D33 — Web: a resume icon button in `SessionHeader`, between Download and Delete.** Owner-only (like share/delete — the CLI's fetch is owner-validated server-side anyway) and visible under the existing `resume` feature flag (`useFlag`). **Enabled only when the session is resumable** (`sessionDataSize > 0`); otherwise disabled with a tooltip ("This session predates resume support — re-sync it from its machine with a current CLI to enable."). The wire already carries `sessionDataSize` (`SessionDetailSchema`, `shared/types.ts:159`; `toSessionSummary`, `worker/supabase.ts:352`) but the frontend drops it — it must be added to `SessionDetail` (`services/api.ts:52-84`) and threaded through `SessionView`'s hand-built `sessionData` prop (`SessionView.tsx:102-117`).
233	+- **D34 — Click: entitled (`can("resume")`) → command dialog; not entitled → navigate to `/resume`.** The `/resume` hub (`App.tsx:321`) is the feature's explanation/upsell page, so it's the richer sell — an intentional divergence from `ResumeButton.tsx`'s inline `promptUpgrade("resume")` pattern.
234	+- **D35 — The dialog auto-copies on open, and shows the command with a copy-again affordance.** Pattern to follow: `ProviderPicker.tsx` (already a Dialog that builds a `specstory resume` command with a copied-state Copy button) plus the shared `copyToClipboard` util (`lib/utils/share.ts:32`, clipboard API + fallback). Content: brief explanation — pasting this in a terminal resumes the session on that machine via the **SpecStory CLI**, which must be installed (link install docs) and logged into SpecStory Cloud (`specstory login`) — then the command in a code block with the Copy button. No agent picker (D32).
235	+- **D36 — The web copies the `specstory://` form, appending `--cloud-url` on non-production origins.** The command is `specstory resume --session specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}` — the canonical, host-free URI (D29), deliberately *not* the page URL, so the copied command carries no host at all and D30's host check never enters the picture for the product-emitted flow. Because the URI is host-free, non-production deployments need the target host expressed some other way: append ` --cloud-url {window.location.origin}` when the origin differs from the production constant `https://cloud.specstory.com`, so cloud-dev/self-hosted copies work with zero manual flags while production commands stay clean. (The frontend has no environment config for this today — `API_BASE = window.location.origin`, `services/api.ts:188` — hence the compare-to-prod-constant approach.) The https permalink form remains supported purely for hand-pasted browser URLs.

15	// Direct session addressing for `specstory resume --session <uri>` (Chunk 5, D28–D36).
16	//
17	// A session can be chosen interactively in the TUI, or now directly via a session URI. The
18	// driving use case is the Cloud web app's Resume button, which copies a paste-able command
19	// carrying exactly the two IDs the cloud API needs (project_id + native session id). The URI
20	// resolves to the same session identity the picker would produce — including D13's
21	// local-preferred selection-time guard — and feeds the identical resumePlan → launchResume
22	// machinery, so there is no parallel resume implementation.
23	
24	// sessionURI is a parsed --session argument: a project id + native session id, plus (for
25	// pasted web permalinks only) the origin the link points at so D30's host check can run.
26	// projectID is empty for the bare-UUID form (resolved local-first, then cloud-discovered).
27	type sessionURI struct {
28		projectID string // "" for a bare session UUID
29		sessionID string // normalized (lowercase) native session uuid
30		host      string // permalink origin (scheme://host[:port]); "" for specstory:// and bare UUID
31	}
32	
33	// Project ids are the CLI-minted truncated-SHA form: xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx (16 hex chars,
34	// createHash in pkg/utils/project_identity.go). Session ids are provider-generated UUIDs:
35	// xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx. Both are matched case-insensitively.
36	var (
37		projectIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}$`)
38		sessionIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`)
39	)
40	
41	// parseSessionURI parses the three accepted --session forms (D29):
42	//
43	//  1. specstory://projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID} — the canonical, host-free form the
44	//     web app copies (D36). url.Parse puts "projects" in Host for a custom scheme, so host+path
45	//     are rejoined before matching.
46	//  2. https://{host}/projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID} — a pasted browser permalink.
47	//     Trailing slashes are tolerated and any path segments after the session id (e.g.
48	//     /chats/{chatId}) are ignored, so any session-page URL pastes cleanly.
49	//  3. {sessionUUID} — bare session id shorthand; resolves local-first then cloud.
50	//
51	// ID shapes are validated up front for early, clear errors.
52	func parseSessionURI(raw string) (sessionURI, error) {
53		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
54		if raw == "" {
55			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: "--session requires a session URI or UUID"}
56		}
57	
58		// A bare UUID has no scheme delimiter. Detect it before url.Parse (which would treat it as a
59		// path and lose nothing, but validating the shape here gives the clearest error).
60		if !strings.Contains(raw, "://") && sessionIDRe.MatchString(raw) {
61			return sessionURI{sessionID: strings.ToLower(raw)}, nil
62		}
63	
64		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
65		if err != nil {
66			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf("invalid session URI %q: %v", raw, err)}
67		}
68	
69		switch u.Scheme {
70		case "specstory":
71			// For a custom (non-special) scheme, url.Parse lands "projects" in Host and the rest in
72			// Path. Rejoin them so the /projects/{id}/sessions/{id} grammar matches the permalink form.
73			segs := pathSegments(u.Host + u.Path)
74			uri, ok := matchSessionPath(segs)
75			if !ok {
76				return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
77					"invalid specstory: URI %q — expected specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}", raw)}
78			}
79			return uri, nil
80		case "http", "https":
81			segs := pathSegments(u.Path)
82			uri, ok := matchSessionPath(segs)
83			if !ok {
84				return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
85					"invalid session URL %q — expected /projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}", raw)}
86			}
87			uri.host = u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host
88			return uri, nil
89		default:
90			// A bare non-UUID string (or any other scheme): report a shape error rather than silently
91			// treating garbage as a session id.
92			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
93				"unsupported session URI %q — use specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}, a cloud permalink, or a session UUID", raw)}
94		}
95	}
96	
97	// matchSessionPath validates the /projects/{pid}/sessions/{sid}[/…] segment grammar and returns
98	// the parsed URI (shapes validated, ids lowercased) or ok=false.
99	func matchSessionPath(segs []string) (sessionURI, bool) {
100		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[0] != "projects" || segs[2] != "sessions" {
101			return sessionURI{}, false
102		}
103		pid, sid := segs[1], segs[3]
104		if !projectIDRe.MatchString(pid) {
105			return sessionURI{}, false
106		}
107		if !sessionIDRe.MatchString(sid) {
108			return sessionURI{}, false
109		}
110		return sessionURI{
111			projectID: strings.ToLower(pid),
112			sessionID: strings.ToLower(sid),
113		}, true
114	}
115	
116	// pathSegments splits a URL path (or rejoined host+path) on "/" and drops empty segments, so
117	// trailing slashes ("/…/sessions/sid/") and any "/chats/{id}" tail collapse to the same token
118	// stream as the canonical form.
119	func pathSegments(s string) []string {
120		parts := strings.Split(s, "/")
121		out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
122		for _, p := range parts {
123			if p != "" {
124				out = append(out, p)
125			}
126		}
127		return out
128	}
129	
130	// resolveSessionURI resolves a --session argument to a sessionindex.Session ready for resume,
131	// applying D31's resolution order and D30's host check:
132	//
133	//  1. Local index first: look the session id up across all agents. A hit means an in-place
134	//     local resume using the row's agent/origin_cwd — exactly like D13's guard. This also makes
135	//     a pasted CLOUD permalink resume locally (offline) when the session exists on this machine.
136	//  2. Else cloud, gated by D10 eligibility surfaced as actionable errors: not logged in → the
137	//     login message; a 403 → the "requires SpecStory Pro" mapping. With a project id in hand,
138	//     the session summary is fetched directly; a bare UUID discovers the owning project via the
139	//     current project's cloud list, then the all-projects ?resumable=true listing.
140	//  3. Else a "session not found" error naming where it looked.
141	//
142	// The cloud summary (not the SessionData blob) supplies the agent/machine attribution the
143	// resumePlan and TUI need; the blob fetch happens later, once, in prepareCloudResumeTarget.
144	func resolveSessionURI(
145		raw string,
146		store *sessionindex.Store,
147		homeProjectID string,
148		agentIDByName map[string]string,
149	) (*sessionindex.Session, error) {
150		uri, err := parseSessionURI(raw)
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, err
153		}
154	
155		// D30: a pasted permalink contributes IDs only — the Bearer token never goes to the
156		// permalink's host. If it differs from the configured cloud host, refuse and point at
157		// --cloud-url. specstory:// and bare-UUID forms carry no host, so the check is skipped.
158		if uri.host != "" {
159			configured := cloud.GetAPIBaseURL()
160			if !strings.EqualFold(uri.host, configured) {
161				return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
162					"This link points at %s, but the CLI is configured for %s. Pass --cloud-url %s if this is intentional.",
163					uri.host, configured, uri.host)}
164			}
165		}
166	
167		// (1) Local-first: a session present on this machine resumes in place, offline.
168		if local, ok, lerr := store.GetSessionByID(uri.sessionID); lerr != nil {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("looking up session locally: %w", lerr)
170		} else if ok {
171			return &local, nil
172		}
173	
174		// (2) Cloud. Not-logged-in is surfaced up front; Pro is surfaced via the API's 403.
175		if !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
176			return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: "Log into SpecStory Cloud (specstory login) to resume sessions from your other machines."}
177		}
178	
179		var (
180			cs        *cloud.CloudSession
181			projectID string
182		)
183		if uri.projectID != "" {
184			cs, err = findCloudSessionInProject(uri.projectID, uri.sessionID)
185			if err != nil {
186				return nil, mapCloudResumeErr(err)
187			}
188			projectID = uri.projectID
189		} else {
190			// Bare UUID: try the current project first, then discover across all projects.
191			cs, err = findCloudSessionInProject(homeProjectID, uri.sessionID)
192			if err != nil {
193				return nil, mapCloudResumeErr(err)
194			}
195			if cs != nil {
196				projectID = homeProjectID
197			} else {
198				cs, projectID, err = findCloudSessionAnywhere(uri.sessionID)
199				if err != nil {
200					return nil, mapCloudResumeErr(err)
201				}
202			}
203		}
204	
205		if cs == nil {
206			return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
207				"session %s not found locally or in SpecStory Cloud", shortID(uri.sessionID))}
208		}
209	
210		// Convert the cloud summary to an index row (resolves the agent from its display name).
211		rows := cloudToSessions([]cloud.CloudSession{*cs}, agentIDByName)
212		if len(rows) == 0 {
213			return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
214				"session %s is from an agent this CLI doesn't know (%q)", shortID(uri.sessionID), cs.Metadata.AgentName)}
215		}
216		s := rows[0]
217		// The per-project cloud list omits projectId (context supplies it); restore it from the
218		// resolved project so the resumePlan and cloud fetch key on the right project.
219		if projectID != "" {
220			s.ProjectID = projectID
221		}
222		return &s, nil
223	}
224	
225	// findCloudSessionInProject lists a project's resumable cloud sessions and returns the one whose
226	// native session id (clientId) matches, or nil if none. The per-project list is capped at 500 by
227	// the server, so this is a cheap linear scan over the same summaries the browse picker uses.
228	func findCloudSessionInProject(projectID, sessionID string) (*cloud.CloudSession, error) {
229		if projectID == "" {
230			return nil, nil
231		}
232		sessions, err := cloud.ListCloudSessions(projectID)
233		if err != nil {
234			return nil, err
235		}
236		return cloudSessionByID(sessions, sessionID), nil
237	}
238	
239	// findCloudSessionAnywhere discovers the owning project for a bare session id via the all-projects
240	// ?resumable=true listing (D24 embeds every resumable session in one request). Returns the
241	// matching summary and its project id, or (nil, "", nil) when the id isn't in any project.
242	func findCloudSessionAnywhere(sessionID string) (*cloud.CloudSession, string, error) {
243		projects, err := cloud.ListCloudProjects()
244		if err != nil {
245			return nil, "", err
246		}
247		for _, p := range projects {
248			if cs := cloudSessionByID(p.Sessions, sessionID); cs != nil {
249				// The embedded summaries carry their projectId (derived from the workspace row), so
250				// prefer it when present; fall back to the project's own id for safety.
251				pid := cs.ProjectID
252				if pid == "" {
253					pid = p.ID
254				}
255				return cs, pid, nil
256			}
257		}
258		return nil, "", nil
259	}
260	
261	// cloudSessionByID returns a pointer to the first session in cs whose clientId matches id, or nil.
262	func cloudSessionByID(cs []cloud.CloudSession, id string) *cloud.CloudSession {
263		for i := range cs {
264			if strings.EqualFold(cs[i].ClientID, id) {
265				return &cs[i]
266			}
267		}
268		return nil
269	}
270	
271	// mapCloudResumeErr converts cloud API errors from the resolution path into the actionable,
272	// D31-worded messages a non-TUI caller prints. A 401 (expired/missing token) → the login nudge;
273	// a 403 / "upgrade_required" → the Pro message (mirroring FetchSessionData's mapping); anything
274	// else passes through unwrapped so genuine network/server failures still read clearly.
275	func mapCloudResumeErr(err error) error {
276		if err == nil {
277			return nil
278		}
279		var authErr *cloud.ErrAuthenticationFailed
280		if errors.As(err, &authErr) {
281			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "Log into SpecStory Cloud (specstory login) to resume sessions from your other machines."}
282		}
283		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "upgrade_required") {
284			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "Resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro."}
285		}
286		return err
287	}

267	// skillsAPIRequest performs an authenticated JSON request to the cloud skills surface and
268	// decodes the response into out. It centralizes the auth header, envelope handling, and
269	// 401 -> ErrAuthenticationFailed mapping shared by every skills call (the rest of the

271	// shared helper keeps them DRY). reqBody is JSON-marshaled when non-nil.
272	func skillsAPIRequest(method, path string, reqBody any, out any) error {
273		apiURL := GetAPIBaseURL() + path
274	
275		var bodyReader io.Reader
276		if reqBody != nil {
277			data, err := json.Marshal(reqBody)
278			if err != nil {
279				return fmt.Errorf("encoding request body: %w", err)
280			}
281			bodyReader = bytes.NewBuffer(data)
282		}
283	
284		req, err := http.NewRequest(method, apiURL, bodyReader)
285		if err != nil {
286			return fmt.Errorf("creating %s request: %w", method, err)
287		}
288		req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+GetCloudToken())
289		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
290		req.Header.Set("User-Agent", GetUserAgent())
291		if reqBody != nil {
292			req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
293		}
294	
295		client := &http.Client{Timeout: skillsHTTPTimeout}
296		resp, err := client.Do(req)
297		if err != nil {
298			return fmt.Errorf("%s %s failed: %w", method, path, err)
299		}
300		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
301	
302		respBody, err := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
303		if err != nil {
304			return fmt.Errorf("reading response body: %w", err)
305		}
306	
307		// A 401 is surfaced as the package's typed auth error so callers can prompt re-login
308		// the same way the rest of the cloud code does.
309		if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized {
310			slog.Debug("skills API unauthorized", "path", path, "status", resp.StatusCode)
311			return &ErrAuthenticationFailed{Message: "not authenticated to SpecStory Cloud"}
312		}
313		if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
314			slog.Debug("skills API non-2xx", "path", path, "status", resp.StatusCode, "body", string(respBody))
315			// Surface the server's own error message when present ({success:false, error:"..."}),
316			// so 403 upgrade_required / 409 already-in-progress read clearly to the user.
317			var envelope struct {
318				Error string `json:"error"`
319			}
320			if json.Unmarshal(respBody, &envelope) == nil && envelope.Error != "" {
321				return fmt.Errorf("%s", envelope.Error)
322			}
323			return fmt.Errorf("%s %s returned status %d", method, path, resp.StatusCode)
324		}
325	
326		if out != nil {
327			if err := json.Unmarshal(respBody, out); err != nil {
328				return fmt.Errorf("parsing response from %s: %w", path, err)
329			}
330		}
331		return nil

// agentIDByNameFromRegistry builds the agent display-name → provider-id map that cloud row
// conversion (cloudToSessions) needs to resolve a cloud session's metadata.agentName back to
// the provider id the resume/reconstruct path keys on. Mirrors the map newSessionTUI builds
// from the TUI's agentMeta set, but from the registry alone so non-TUI callers (--session)// can build it without constructing a picker.
func agentIDByNameFromRegistry(registry *factory.Registry) map[string]string {
	out := make(map[string]string)
	for _, id := range registry.ListIDs() {
		prov, err := registry.Get(id)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		out[prov.Name()] = id
	}
	return out
}

// resumePlanFromSession builds a resumePlan for a directly-resolved session (the --session path
// with a preset agent), reusing the same selection-time guard and plan shape as the TUI tail.

	}

## Most important improvements

1. **(37) Fix the bare-UUID discovery abort** — the strongest candidate is deleting `findCloudSessionInProject` from the bare-UUID branch entirely (38): the anywhere-scan already covers the current project, uncapped, in one request. As written, the feature's shorthand form fails with a raw 404 in any directory whose project isn't in the cloud — including every "unknown" project.
2. **(36) Move the D30 host check after the local lookup.** The token-protection property only matters when a cloud call is about to happen; checking first breaks offline local resume via a mismatched-host permalink, which the design doc explicitly promises works.
3. **(39) Close the >500-sessions hole in the direct path** — fall back to `findCloudSessionAnywhere` when the capped project list misses, or add a single-session summary read. Right now the *canonical web-copied URI* is the least reliable form for big projects.
4. **(11)+(12) Observability**: add a `"via"` property to `EventResumeActivated` and `slog.Debug` lines for parse/resolution outcomes. This feature exists to power a web funnel; today you can't see it being used.
5. **(10) Deduplicate the RunE tail** — resolve into a `pinned` variable and fall through to the one existing `selectResumeViaTUI → launchResume` tail, keeping the single-exit shape.

## Unit tests

The new `TestParseSessionURI` is exactly the right kind of test — data-driven, pure, pinning real grammar/normalization logic (49–52). Two additions worth making, both testing genuine logic rather than coverage:

- **`GetSessionByID` collision tiebreak** (store.go): insert two rows with the same `session_id` under different agents plus a deleted third, assert the most-recent live row wins. That's the one behavior the SQL `ORDER BY … LIMIT 1` + `deleted = 0` encodes, and it's cheap with the existing in-memory store test setup.
- **Resolution-order logic**: `resolveSessionURI` as written isn't unit-testable (concrete `*Store`, package-level cloud calls). I would *not* mock the cloud for it — but if you adopt improvement 2, the host-mismatch rule becomes a small pure function (`uriHost` vs configured) that can join the parse table. The end-to-end resolution paths are better covered by the doc's manual validation list.

Not worth testing: `pathSegments`/`cloudSessionByID` in isolation (trivial), and nothing about `url.Parse` itself — the existing table already exercises it only through our grammar.

One process note: the diff also rewraps help text in four unrelated commands (5) — consider splitting that into its own commit so this change stays reviewable as Chunk 5.

15	// Direct session addressing for `specstory resume --session <uri>` (Chunk 5, D28–D36).
16	//
17	// A session can be chosen interactively in the TUI, or now directly via a session URI. The
18	// driving use case is the Cloud web app's Resume button, which copies a paste-able command
19	// carrying exactly the two IDs the cloud API needs (project_id + native session id). The URI
20	// resolves to the same session identity the picker would produce — including D13's
21	// local-preferred selection-time guard — and feeds the identical resumePlan → launchResume
22	// machinery, so there is no parallel resume implementation.
23	
24	// sessionURI is a parsed --session argument: a project id + native session id, plus (for
25	// pasted web permalinks only) the origin the link points at so D30's host check can run.
26	// projectID is empty for the bare-UUID form (resolved local-first, then cloud-discovered).
27	type sessionURI struct {
28		projectID string // "" for a bare session UUID
29		sessionID string // normalized (lowercase) native session uuid
30		host      string // permalink origin (scheme://host[:port]); "" for specstory:// and bare UUID
31	}
32	
33	// Project ids are the CLI-minted truncated-SHA form: xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx (16 hex chars,
34	// createHash in pkg/utils/project_identity.go). Session ids are provider-generated UUIDs:
35	// xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx. Both are matched case-insensitively.
36	var (
37		projectIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}$`)
38		sessionIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`)
39	)
40	
41	// parseSessionURI parses the three accepted --session forms (D29):
42	//
43	//  1. specstory://projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID} — the canonical, host-free form the
44	//     web app copies (D36). url.Parse puts "projects" in Host for a custom scheme, so host+path
45	//     are rejoined before matching.
46	//  2. https://{host}/projects/{projectID}/sessions/{sessionID} — a pasted browser permalink.
47	//     Trailing slashes are tolerated and any path segments after the session id (e.g.
48	//     /chats/{chatId}) are ignored, so any session-page URL pastes cleanly.
49	//  3. {sessionUUID} — bare session id shorthand; resolves local-first then cloud.
50	//
51	// ID shapes are validated up front for early, clear errors.
52	func parseSessionURI(raw string) (sessionURI, error) {
53		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
54		if raw == "" {
55			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: "--session requires a session URI or UUID"}
56		}
57	
58		// A bare UUID has no scheme delimiter. Detect it before url.Parse (which would treat it as a
59		// path and lose nothing, but validating the shape here gives the clearest error).
60		if !strings.Contains(raw, "://") && sessionIDRe.MatchString(raw) {
61			return sessionURI{sessionID: strings.ToLower(raw)}, nil
62		}
63	
64		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
65		if err != nil {
66			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf("invalid session URI %q: %v", raw, err)}
67		}
68	
69		switch u.Scheme {
70		case "specstory":
71			// For a custom (non-special) scheme, url.Parse lands "projects" in Host and the rest in
72			// Path. Rejoin them so the /projects/{id}/sessions/{id} grammar matches the permalink form.
73			segs := pathSegments(u.Host + u.Path)
74			uri, ok := matchSessionPath(segs)
75			if !ok {
76				return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
77					"invalid specstory: URI %q — expected specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}", raw)}
78			}
79			return uri, nil
80		case "http", "https":
81			segs := pathSegments(u.Path)
82			uri, ok := matchSessionPath(segs)
83			if !ok {
84				return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
85					"invalid session URL %q — expected /projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}", raw)}
86			}
87			uri.host = u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host
88			return uri, nil
89		default:
90			// A bare non-UUID string (or any other scheme): report a shape error rather than silently
91			// treating garbage as a session id.
92			return sessionURI{}, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
93				"unsupported session URI %q — use specstory://projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sessionId}, a cloud permalink, or a session UUID", raw)}
94		}
95	}
96	
97	// matchSessionPath validates the /projects/{pid}/sessions/{sid}[/…] segment grammar and returns
98	// the parsed URI (shapes validated, ids lowercased) or ok=false.
99	func matchSessionPath(segs []string) (sessionURI, bool) {
100		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[0] != "projects" || segs[2] != "sessions" {
101			return sessionURI{}, false
102		}
103		pid, sid := segs[1], segs[3]
104		if !projectIDRe.MatchString(pid) {
105			return sessionURI{}, false
106		}
107		if !sessionIDRe.MatchString(sid) {
108			return sessionURI{}, false
109		}
110		return sessionURI{
111			projectID: strings.ToLower(pid),
112			sessionID: strings.ToLower(sid),
113		}, true
114	}
115	
116	// pathSegments splits a URL path (or rejoined host+path) on "/" and drops empty segments, so
117	// trailing slashes ("/…/sessions/sid/") and any "/chats/{id}" tail collapse to the same token
118	// stream as the canonical form.
119	func pathSegments(s string) []string {
120		parts := strings.Split(s, "/")
121		out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
122		for _, p := range parts {
123			if p != "" {
124				out = append(out, p)
125			}
126		}
127		return out
128	}

130	// resolveSessionURI resolves a --session argument to a sessionindex.Session ready for resume,
131	// applying D31's resolution order and D30's host check:
132	//
133	//  1. Local index first: look the session id up across all agents. A hit means an in-place
134	//     local resume using the row's agent/origin_cwd — exactly like D13's guard. This also makes
135	//     a pasted CLOUD permalink resume locally (offline) when the session exists on this machine.
136	//  2. Else cloud, gated by D10 eligibility surfaced as actionable errors: not logged in → the
137	//     login message; a 403 → the "requires SpecStory Pro" mapping. With a project id in hand,
138	//     the session summary is fetched directly; a bare UUID discovers the owning project via the
139	//     current project's cloud list, then the all-projects ?resumable=true listing.
140	//  3. Else a "session not found" error naming where it looked.
141	//
142	// The cloud summary (not the SessionData blob) supplies the agent/machine attribution the
143	// resumePlan and TUI need; the blob fetch happens later, once, in prepareCloudResumeTarget.
144	func resolveSessionURI(
145		raw string,
146		store *sessionindex.Store,
147		agentIDByName map[string]string,
148	) (*sessionindex.Session, error) {
149		uri, err := parseSessionURI(raw)
150		if err != nil {
151			return nil, err
152		}
153	
154		// (1) Local-first: a session present on this machine resumes in place, offline. This runs
155		// BEFORE the D30 host check on purpose — a pasted cloud-dev permalink for a session that
156		// exists locally should resume offline without tripping the host-mismatch guard. The check
157		// only needs to gate the cloud call below (the token never goes to the permalink's host);
158		// a local hit makes no cloud call at all.
159		if local, ok, lerr := store.GetSessionByID(uri.sessionID); lerr != nil {
160			return nil, fmt.Errorf("looking up session locally: %w", lerr)
161		} else if ok {
162			return &local, nil
163		}
164	
165		// D30: a pasted permalink contributes IDs only — the Bearer token never goes to the

169		if uri.host != "" {
170			configured := cloud.GetAPIBaseURL()
171			if !strings.EqualFold(uri.host, configured) {
172				return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
173					"This link points at %s, but the CLI is configured for %s. Pass --cloud-url %s if this is intentional.",
174					uri.host, configured, uri.host)}
175			}
176		}
177	
178		// (2) Cloud. Not-logged-in is surfaced up front; Pro is surfaced via the API's 403.
179		if !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
180			return nil, utils.ValidationError{Message: "Log into SpecStory Cloud (specstory login) to resume sessions from your other machines."}
181		}
182	
183		var (
184			cs        *cloud.CloudSession
185			projectID string
186		)
187		if uri.projectID != "" {
188			// Direct form: recover the session summary from the named project. The per-project list

213			cs, projectID, err = findCloudSessionAnywhere(uri.sessionID)

217		}

222		}

239	// findCloudSessionInProject lists a project's resumable cloud sessions and returns the one whose
240	// native session id (clientId) matches, or nil if none. NOTE: the per-project list is capped at
241	// cloudResumeLimit (500) by the server, so a resumable session older than the project's newest 500
242	// misses it — callers that must not miss should fall back to findCloudSessionAnywhere (uncapped).
243	func findCloudSessionInProject(projectID, sessionID string) (*cloud.CloudSession, error) {
244		if projectID == "" {
245			return nil, nil
246		}
247		sessions, err := cloud.ListCloudSessions(projectID)
248		if err != nil {
249			return nil, err
250		}

252	}

254	// findCloudSessionAnywhere discovers the owning project for a bare session id via the all-projects
255	// ?resumable=true listing (D24 embeds every resumable session in one request). Returns the
256	// matching summary and its project id, or (nil, "", nil) when the id isn't in any project.
257	func findCloudSessionAnywhere(sessionID string) (*cloud.CloudSession, string, error) {
258		projects, err := cloud.ListCloudProjects()
259		if err != nil {
260			return nil, "", err
261		}
262		for _, p := range projects {
263			if cs := cloudSessionByID(p.Sessions, sessionID); cs != nil {
264				// The embedded summaries carry their projectId (derived from the workspace row), so

A mismatched-host permalink for a locally-present session now resumes offline, and the comment explains exactly why the ordering is deliberate — the check only needs to gate the cloud call. This is the fix done right, not just moved code.

The "unknown"-project 404 abort is eliminated.
- **(39) The direct `(projectId, sessionId)` form falls back to the uncapped all-projects scan on a miss** (`session_uri.go:187-208`), with the 500-row cap documented both at the call site and on `findCloudSessionInProject` itself. The fix also adds a guard I'd endorse: a fallback match in a *different* project than the URI named is treated as not-found (the URI's project is authoritative) — correct handling of the stale/wrong-URI case rather than silently resuming something else.

One small residue of (39) remains: if the *named project itself* doesn't exist in the cloud, `ListCloudSessions` errors (404) and surfaces raw ("returned status 404") without trying the fallback — only the "project exists but session missed the cap" case falls through. // first-exchange lookup (sequential Supabase round-trips that would make the resume browse
// chronically slow on large projects; the CLI never uses exchangeCount/firstExchangeContent).
// Ordered by real activity (ended_at, then updated_at) so every resume surface sorts the same
// way. Callers add their own scoping (e.g. .limit()).
function resumableSessionsQuery(workspaceIds: string[]) {
  return supabaseClient()
    .from("sessions")
    .select(
      "id, client_id, workspace_id, name, user_title, markdown_size, raw_data_size, session_data_size, created_at, updated_at, started_at, ended_at, metadata"
    )
    .in("workspace_id", workspaceIds)
    .gt("session_data_size", 0)
    .order("ended_at", { ascending: false, nullsFirst: false })
    .order("updated_at", { ascending: false });
}

// need every resumable session, and the fetch is a one-shot on entering the browser.

  const workspaceIds = await getAccessibleWorkspaceIds(request.userId!);

    .from("workspaces")
    .select("id, project_id, owner_id, name, icon, color, created_at, updated_at")
    .in("id", workspaceIds);

**What scope should the cap removal cover?**

Options:
- **All cloud reads (Recommended)** - Uncap cloud browse, cloud search, and URI resolution (delete cloudResumeLimit; server serves complete resumable lists via paging). Local search's LIMIT 500 stays — it bounds a search-results view, not data availability.
- **URI resolution only** - Keep D21's 500 for the browse/search pickers; make only --session resolution exact and capless. Smallest change, but the picker still silently hides sessions past 500 in big projects.
- **Everything incl. local search** - Also drop the local FTS LIMIT 500 so local and cloud match at 'no cap'. Full D21 repeal; TUI result lists can get very large.

**How should the server serve unbounded resumable lists (PostgREST silently truncates unpaged queries at its Max Rows setting)?**

Options:
- **Page with .range() (Recommended)** - Loop .range() in the two resumable query helpers until short page. Robust regardless of the Supabase Max Rows setting; also fixes the existing silent ~1000-row truncation of the 'deliberately no limit' all-projects listing (D25).
- **Raise Supabase Max Rows** - Bump the project's Max Rows config and keep single unpaged queries. No code loop, but the ceiling is just higher and hidden in dashboard config — breaks again at the new number.


**Answer:** All cloud reads (Recommended), Page with .range() (Recommended)

36:- **D21 — Cloud results are capped at 500 (recency), matching local; no paging.** Both cloud browse (`GET …/sessions`) and cloud search use `limit = 500` — the same bound as local search (`LIMIT 500` by recency) — so each source contributes its 500 newest, they merge and dedup (local preferred), and there is **no** "load more" affordance. Simplest model; matches today's local behavior.
102:- **`search` read path:** FTS5 `MATCH` over `name`+`body`, joined back to `sessions`, newest-first, LIMIT 500 (`store.go:545`); snippet highlighting lazily for visible rows (`store.go:581`).
180:2. **Server-side FTS already exists** (`searchSessions` GraphQL over `exchanges.fts`). ⇒ **Cloud-search is feasible** without new infra. But ranking/tokenization differs from local: cloud = Postgres `websearch_to_tsquery` over parsed exchanges, ranked by recency-of-match; local = SQLite FTS5 over a flattened body, LIMIT 500 by recency. **Gap (since addressed):** merge/dedup and alignment strategy — resolved by D13 (blend/dedup), D17 (recency ordering), D18 (aligned `simple` FTS).
256:- **List (`GET …/{projectId}/sessions`)** — new opt-in **`?resumable=true`** param → filter `WHERE session_data_size > 0` (omitted = today's behavior, so the web app is untouched); return `metadata` (for the machine badge/filter); the CLI passes `limit=500` as a request param — the endpoint's default (200) is unchanged for the web app (D5/D9/D21).
258:- **Aligned search** — a **new endpoint** (own pathname → own rate-limit bucket, D18): build `to_tsquery('simple', …)` mirroring `ftsQuery` (implicit AND, phrase `<->`, last-token `:*`) against `exchanges.fts_simple` — constructive tokenization only (no raw input reaches the tsquery parser), empty token list short-circuits to zero hits, errors return empty rather than 500 (D18); filter `session_data_size > 0`; return **`ts_headline`** snippets delimited with STX/ETX to match local `snippet()`; sort by recency; `limit = 500` (D17/D18/D19/D21). Kept separate from the web app's `english` `searchSessions`.
298:- **Server:** stream-`SessionData` read endpoint (`downloadFromStorage`, D8); `?resumable=true` on list + return `metadata`, `limit 500` (D5/D9/D21); reuse `GET /api/v1/projects` for blended projects (D16).
306:- **Server:** `exchanges.fts_simple` plain column + `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` trigger + GIN index (no backfill, D20); aligned search as a dedicated endpoint (own rate-limit bucket) — `to_tsquery('simple', …)` mirroring `ftsQuery` (D18), `ts_headline` snippets delimiter-matched to local (D19), recency sort + `limit 500` (D17/D21), `session_data_size > 0` filter.
308:- **Validation:** compare local vs cloud results for the same queries (stemming/stopword/prefix parity per D18); confirm snippets render identically, recency ordering across sources, the 500 cap, and that `fts_simple` populated via re-sync (no backfill run).

+import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
+import { Copy, Check, RotateCcw } from "lucide-react";
+import {
+  Dialog,
+  DialogContent,
+  DialogHeader,
+  DialogTitle,
+  DialogDescription,
+} from "@/ui-components/ui/dialog";
+import { copyToClipboard } from "@/lib/utils/share";
+
+/**
+ * Build the `specstory resume --session` command for a session (D35/D36). Uses the canonical,
+ * host-free `specstory://` URI — never the page URL — so the copied command carries no host at
+ * all. Users of dev/staging clouds already point their CLI at the right server (via --cloud-url
+ * or SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL), so the copied command never needs to carry one; it's the same clean
+ * form in every environment.
+ */
+function buildResumeCommand(projectId: string, sessionId: string): string {
+  return `specstory resume --session specstory://projects/${projectId}/sessions/${sessionId}`;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Resume-command dialog for the session page's Resume button (D35). Auto-copies the command on
+ * open, shows it in a code block with a copy-again affordance, and explains that pasting it in a
+ * terminal resumes the session on that machine via the SpecStory CLI (which must be installed and
+ * logged into SpecStory Cloud). No agent picker — the terminal owns target choice (D32).
+ */
+export function ResumeCommandDialog({
+  open,
+  onClose,
+  projectId,
+  sessionId,
+  sessionName,
+}: {
+  open: boolean;
+  onClose: () => void;
+  projectId: string;
+  sessionId: string;
+  sessionName: string;
+}) {
+  const command = buildResumeCommand(projectId, sessionId);
+  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false);
+
+  // Auto-copy on open so the command is already on the clipboard the moment the dialog appears.
+  // Re-runs only when the dialog transitions to open (not on every re-render while open).
+  useEffect(() => {
+    if (!open) {
+      setCopied(false);
+      return;
+    }
+    let cancelled = false;
+    copyToClipboard(command).then((ok) => {
+      if (!cancelled && ok) setCopied(true);
+    });
+    return () => {
+      cancelled = true;
+    };
+  }, [open, command]);
+
+  const copyAgain = async () => {
+    const ok = await copyToClipboard(command);
+    if (ok) {
+      setCopied(true);
+      setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), 2000);
+    }
+  };
+
+  return (
+    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={(o) => !o && onClose()}>
+      <DialogContent
+        className="overflow-hidden"
+        style={{ width: "min(32rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))" }}
+      >
+        <DialogHeader className="min-w-0">
+          <DialogTitle className="flex items-center gap-2 text-base">
+            <RotateCcw size={16} className="text-brand flex-shrink-0" /> Resume session
+          </DialogTitle>
+          <DialogDescription className="break-words">
+            Paste this command into a terminal on the computer where you want to continue the
+            session.
+            {sessionName && (
+              <>
+                {" "}
+                <span className="font-semibold text-foreground">{sessionName}</span>
+              </>
+            )}
+          </DialogDescription>
+        </DialogHeader>
+
+        <div className="mt-1">
+          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
+            <code className="flex-1 rounded-md bg-muted px-3 py-2 font-mono text-xs text-foreground break-all">
+              {command}
+            </code>
+            <button
+              type="button"
+              onClick={copyAgain}
+              className="flex-shrink-0 inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-md border border-border px-2.5 py-2 text-xs text-foreground hover:bg-muted"
+            >
+              {copied ? <Check size={13} className="text-brand" /> : <Copy size={13} />}
+              {copied ? "Copied" : "Copy"}
+            </button>
+          </div>
+          <ul className="mt-3 space-y-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground list-disc list-inside">
+            <li>
+              Requires the{" "}
+              <a
+                href="https://docs.specstory.com/cloud/quickstart"
+                target="_blank"
+                rel="noopener noreferrer"
+                className="underline hover:text-foreground"
+              >
+                SpecStory CLI
+              </a>{" "}
+              installed on that machine.
+            </li>
+            <li>
+              Be sure to login to SpecStory Cloud with{" "}
+              <code className="font-mono">specstory login</code> first.
+            </li>
+          </ul>
+        </div>
+      </DialogContent>
+    </Dialog>
+  );
+}

import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

interface TooltipProps {
  children: ReactNode;
  content: string;
  side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right";
  className?: string;
  theme?: "light" | "dark";
  fixed?: boolean;
}

export function Tooltip({
  children,
  content,
  side = "bottom",
  className,
  theme = "dark",
}: TooltipProps) {
  // Position classes based on side
  const positionClasses = {
    top: "-top-8 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2",
    bottom: "-bottom-8 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2",
    left: "top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 -left-2 -translate-x-full",
    right: "top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 -right-2 translate-x-full",
  };

  return (
    <div className="relative inline-flex">
      <div className="peer">{children}</div>
      <span
        className={cn(
          `absolute px-2 py-1 text-xs rounded-md whitespace-nowrap ${theme === "light" ? "bg-white border border-gray-200 text-gray-700" : "bg-gray-800 border border-gray-700 text-gray-100"}`,
          "opacity-0 peer-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity duration-200",
          "pointer-events-none z-[1000] shadow-lg",
          positionClasses[side],
          className
        )}
      >
        {content}
      </span>
    </div>
  );
}

// Simple wrapper for tooltip trigger elements
export function TooltipTrigger({
  children,
  className,
}: {
  children: ReactNode;
  className?: string;
}) {
  return <div className={className}>{children}</div>;
}

**The D36 deviation (W11) is the one decision item.** As agreed, non-prod origins would append `--cloud-url {origin}`; the implementation instead ships one clean command everywhere and relies on dev users having configured their CLI. It's genuinely defensible — no prod-origin constant to maintain, `SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL` exists for exactly this, and the `specstory://` form triggers no host check — and the failure mode is dev-only (a default-configured CLI resolves against prod and reports "session not found" instead of pointing at cloud-dev). I lean **accept and amend D36** to document the simplification and its failure mode, but it's your product call — say the word and I'll either amend the doc or flag the code for fixing to spec.

**One cross-cutting miss I own:** your standing feedback says code comments must be self-contained and never cite decision IDs or chunk numbers — and both implementations are full of `(D33)`, `(Chunk 5, D28–D36)` references (web: `SessionHeader.tsx`, `ResumeCommandDialog.tsx`; CLI: `session_uri.go`, `resume.go`, `session_tui.go`). I should have caught that in the CLI review. Worth a sweep in both repos to reword those comments to say what they mean in place.

import { useState } from "react";
import { Copy, Check, RotateCcw } from "lucide-react";
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogDescription,
} from "@/ui-components/ui/dialog";
import { buildResumeCommand, copyToClipboard } from "@/lib/utils/share";

/**
 * Resume-command dialog for the session Resume button (D35). The command is already on the
 * clipboard when this opens — the Resume button copies it synchronously inside its click handler
 * (the user-activation gesture, so Safari can't reject the clipboard write) and passes
 * `initialCopied` so the dialog opens showing "Copied". This dialog is purely presentational:
 * it shows the command and offers a copy-again affordance. No agent picker — the terminal owns
 * target choice (D32).
 */
export function ResumeCommandDialog({
  open,
  onClose,
  projectId,
  sessionId,
  sessionName,
  initialCopied = false,
}: {
  open: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  projectId: string;
  sessionId: string;
  sessionName: string;
  initialCopied?: boolean;
}) {
  const command = buildResumeCommand(projectId, sessionId);
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(initialCopied);

  const copyAgain = async () => {
    const ok = await copyToClipboard(command);
    if (ok) {
      setCopied(true);
      setTimeout(() => setCopied(false), 2000);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={(o) => !o && onClose()}>
      <DialogContent
        className="overflow-hidden"
        style={{ width: "min(32rem, calc(100vw - 2rem))" }}
        // Disable click-outside-to-dismiss. Radix closes on the overlay's pointerdown and
        // unmounts the overlay before the click event resolves, so the click "falls through"
        // to the session card behind the dialog and triggers navigation. Escape and the X
        // button still dismiss (and are clearer intents for a command you're reading).
        onInteractOutside={(e) => e.preventDefault()}
      >
        <DialogHeader className="min-w-0">
          <DialogTitle className="flex items-center gap-2 text-base">
            <RotateCcw size={16} className="text-brand flex-shrink-0" /> Resume session
          </DialogTitle>
          <DialogDescription className="break-words">
            Paste this command into a terminal on the computer where you want to continue the
            session.
            {sessionName && (
              <>
                {" "}
                <span className="font-semibold text-foreground">{sessionName}</span>
              </>
            )}
          </DialogDescription>
        </DialogHeader>

        <div className="mt-1">
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <code className="flex-1 rounded-md bg-muted px-3 py-2 font-mono text-xs text-foreground break-all">
              {command}
            </code>
            <button
              type="button"
              onClick={copyAgain}
              className="flex-shrink-0 inline-flex items-center gap-1 rounded-md border border-border px-2.5 py-2 text-xs text-foreground hover:bg-muted"
            >
              {copied ? <Check size={13} className="text-brand" /> : <Copy size={13} />}
              {copied ? "Copied" : "Copy"}
            </button>
          </div>
          <ul className="mt-3 space-y-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground list-disc list-inside">
            <li>
              Requires the{" "}
              <a
                href="https://docs.specstory.com/cloud/quickstart"
                target="_blank"
                rel="noopener noreferrer"
                className="underline hover:text-foreground"
              >
                SpecStory CLI
              </a>{" "}
              installed on that machine.
            </li>
            <li>
              Be sure to login to SpecStory Cloud with{" "}
              <code className="font-mono">specstory login</code> first.
            </li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  );
}

import { useState } from "react";
import { RotateCcw } from "lucide-react";
import { useEntitlement } from "@/contexts/EntitlementContext";
import { useFlag } from "@/contexts/FlagsContext";
import { useRouter } from "@/hooks/useRouter";
import { Tooltip } from "@/ui-components/ui/tooltip";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils/classnames";
import { buildResumeCommand, copyToClipboard } from "@/lib/utils/share";
import { ResumeCommandDialog } from "./ResumeCommandDialog";

/**
 * Resume affordance for a session. Used in three places — the session page header (icon
 * button), the project-view session card (compact icon, hover-revealed), and the Resume hub
 * (labelled button) — so the behavior stays identical everywhere:
 *
 *  - Env-flagged (`useFlag("resume")`); returns null when off so callers don't each check.
 *  - Enabled only when the session is cloud-resumable (`sessionDataSize > 0`); otherwise
 *    disabled with a tooltip explaining how to enable it.
 *  - Entitled (`can("resume")`) click → copies the `specstory resume` command to the clipboard
 *    SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the click handler (the user-activation gesture, so Safari can't reject
 *    the write), then opens ResumeCommandDialog already showing "Copied". Non-entitled click →
 *    navigate to /resume (the hub's upsell page).
 *  - Our custom Tooltip only — no native `title=` (would double up with the fancy tooltip).
 *
 * `compact` renders an icon-only affordance for dense rows; the default shows a "Resume" label.
 *
 * Dialog open/close is deferred to the next tick (setTimeout 0) so the overlay's mount/unmount
 * never coincides with the click event dispatch — Radix otherwise unmounts on pointerdown and
 * the subsequent click falls through to the session card behind it, triggering navigation.
 */
export function ResumeButton({
  sessionName,
  projectId,
  clientId,
  sessionDataSize,
  compact = false,
  className,
}: {
  sessionName: string;
  projectId?: string;
  clientId?: string;
  sessionDataSize?: number | null;
  compact?: boolean;
  className?: string;
}) {
  const resumeEnabled = useFlag("resume");
  const { can } = useEntitlement();
  const router = useRouter();
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false);

  if (!resumeEnabled) return null;

  const isResumable = !!sessionDataSize && sessionDataSize > 0;
  const hasIds = !!projectId && !!clientId;

  const handle = (e: React.MouseEvent) => {
    // Resume buttons sit inside clickable session cards/rows. Stop BOTH the React synthetic
    // event (so the card's onClick doesn't fire) and the native event (so document-level native
    // listeners don't see it) — the opening click must not navigate.
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    if (e.nativeEvent && typeof e.nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation === "function") {
      e.nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation();
    }
    if (!hasIds || !isResumable) return;

    if (can("resume")) {
      // Copy inside the user-activation gesture (Safari-safe), then open the dialog deferred so
      // the overlay mounts AFTER this click's event chain resolves (prevents the click from
      // falling through to the card once the overlay unmounts on a later dismiss).
      void copyToClipboard(buildResumeCommand(projectId!, clientId!)).then((ok) => {
        if (ok) setCopied(true);
      });
      setTimeout(() => setOpen(true), 0);
    } else {
      router.push("/resume");
    }
  };

  const close = () => {
    // Defer unmount so the dismiss event (overlay pointerdown / X click / Escape) fully
    // resolves against the still-mounted overlay before we tear the portal down — otherwise the
    // dismiss click can fall through to the session card behind it and trigger navigation.
    setTimeout(() => {
      setOpen(false);
      setCopied(false);
    }, 0);
  };

  const tooltip = isResumable
    ? "Resume this session in an agent"
    : "This session predates resume support — re-sync it from its machine with a current CLI to enable.";

  return (
    <>
      <Tooltip content={tooltip} side="bottom">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={handle}
          disabled={!isResumable}
          className={cn(
            "inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md text-xs font-medium transition-colors text-brand hover:bg-brand/10 disabled:opacity-40 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:hover:bg-transparent",
            compact ? "h-7 w-7 justify-center" : "h-7 px-2.5",
            className,
          )}
        >
          <RotateCcw size={14} className="flex-shrink-0" />
          {!compact && <span>Resume</span>}
        </button>
      </Tooltip>
      {open && hasIds && (
        <ResumeCommandDialog
          open={open}
          onClose={close}
          projectId={projectId!}
          sessionId={clientId!}
          sessionName={sessionName}
          initialCopied={copied}
        />
      )}
    </>
  );
}

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-14 20:08:58Z)**_

I have the definitive answer, verified against the installed Radix source. First the W14 check, then the bug.

## W14 fix — verified good, one residual race

The copy now happens **synchronously inside the button's click handler** (`ResumeButton.handle`) — inside the user-activation gesture, so Safari can't reject it — and the dialog is purely presentational, opening pre-marked via `initialCopied`. That's exactly the right pattern.

One small race remains: `copyToClipboard(...).then(ok => setCopied(ok))` resolves asynchronously, while `setTimeout(() => setOpen(true), 0)` is a macrotask. If the clipboard promise resolves *after* the timeout fires (possible — `writeText` is genuinely async), the dialog mounts with `initialCopied = false`, and since the dialog seeds `useState(initialCopied)`, the later prop change is ignored — it shows "Copy" even though the copy succeeded. Folding the open into the `.then` (`.then(ok => { setCopied(ok); setOpen(true); })`) fixes it — and the fix below makes the `setTimeout` wrapper unnecessary anyway.

## The Radix bug — definitive root cause

**It's React portal event bubbling, not Radix and not the unmount timing.** React propagates synthetic events through the **React component tree**, not the DOM tree — this is a documented `createPortal` caveat: *"An event fired from inside a portal propagates to ancestors in the containing React tree, even if those elements are not ancestors in the DOM tree."* The dialog is rendered inside `ResumeButton` inside the card's `<Card onClick={…}>` in the React tree, so a click on the X — although DOM-wise it lives under `document.body` — dispatches along X → `DialogContent` → `Dialog` → `ResumeButton` → … → **the card's `onClick`**. Navigation fires.

Answering the agent's specific hypotheses, from the actual installed dists:

1. **`DialogPrimitive.Close` does nothing unusual.** It's a plain button: `onClick: composeEventHandlers(props.onClick, () => context.onOpenChange(false))` — `react-dialog/dist/index.mjs:271`. No retargeting, no pointerdown handling.
2. **Nothing in Radix stops propagation.** `grep -c stopPropagation` is **0** in both `react-dialog/dist/index.mjs` and `react-dismissable-layer/dist/index.mjs`. Your `ui-components/ui/dialog.tsx` (stock shadcn) adds none either. So every click inside the portal bubbles to the card.
3. **The `setTimeout(0)` close-defer is irrelevant to the X leak.** React fixes the propagation path at dispatch time — even a synchronous `setOpen(false)` wouldn't stop the card handler (already in the same dispatch) from firing. The defer neither causes nor helps this.
4. **Why only the X leaks:** Escape isn't a click; the opening click is stopped in `handle`; and the overlay's *dismiss* fall-through was a genuinely **different mechanism** the agent already fixed — Radix dismisses on pointerdown-outside, the overlay unmounts before the browser fires the follow-up `click`, and that click hit-tests to the card *directly* (a real DOM event on the card, no portal involved). `onInteractOutside={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` correctly neutralizes that one, and its comment is accurate *for that mechanism*. There were two bugs wearing one trench coat. (Side note: a non-dismissing click on the open overlay should *also* React-bubble to the card — if navigation isn't observed there today it's likely just unnoticed; the fix covers it.)

## The canonical fix

Stop propagation at the portal content boundary — the standard pattern for "Radix anything inside a clickable row/card". In `ui-components/ui/dialog.tsx`, after the `{...props}` spread so it can't be accidentally clobbered (or compose with the consumer's handler):

```tsx
<DialogPrimitive.Content
  ref={ref}
  className={...}
  {...props}
  onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); props.onClick?.(e); }}
  onPointerDown={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); props.onPointerDown?.(e); }}
>
```

Doing it in the shared wrapper fixes every dialog that ever sits inside a clickable parent, not just this one. Add the same to `DialogOverlay` if overlay clicks are confirmed to navigate.

**Cleanup this unlocks in `ResumeButton`:** `close()` becomes a plain `setOpen(false); setCopied(false)` (delete the `setTimeout`), and `handle()` keeps `e.stopPropagation()` (the button itself *is* a DOM child of the card — that one's real) but can drop `stopImmediatePropagation` and the deferred open — move `setOpen(true)` into the clipboard `.then`, which also fixes the `initialCopied` race above. **Keep** `onInteractOutside preventDefault` — it guards the second mechanism, which `stopPropagation` does not address.

1	import { useState } from "react";
2	import { RotateCcw } from "lucide-react";
3	import { useEntitlement } from "@/contexts/EntitlementContext";
4	import { useFlag } from "@/contexts/FlagsContext";
5	import { useRouter } from "@/hooks/useRouter";
6	import { Tooltip } from "@/ui-components/ui/tooltip";
7	import { cn } from "@/lib/utils/classnames";
8	import { buildResumeCommand, copyToClipboard } from "@/lib/utils/share";
9	import { ResumeCommandDialog } from "./ResumeCommandDialog";
10	
11	/**
12	 * Resume affordance for a session. Used in three places — the session page header (icon
13	 * button), the project-view session card (compact icon, hover-revealed), and the Resume hub
14	 * (labelled button) — so the behavior stays identical everywhere:
15	 *
16	 *  - Env-flagged (`useFlag("resume")`); returns null when off so callers don't each check.
17	 *  - Enabled only when the session is cloud-resumable (`sessionDataSize > 0`); otherwise
18	 *    disabled with a tooltip explaining how to enable it.
19	 *  - Entitled (`can("resume")`) click → copies the `specstory resume` command to the clipboard
20	 *    SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the click handler (the user-activation gesture, so Safari can't reject
21	 *    the write), then opens ResumeCommandDialog already showing "Copied". Non-entitled click →
22	 *    navigate to /resume (the hub's upsell page).
23	 *  - Our custom Tooltip only — no native `title=` (would double up with the fancy tooltip).
24	 *
25	 * `compact` renders an icon-only affordance for dense rows; the default shows a "Resume" label.
26	 *
27	 * Dialog open/close is deferred to the next tick (setTimeout 0) so the overlay's mount/unmount
28	 * never coincides with the click event dispatch — Radix otherwise unmounts on pointerdown and
29	 * the subsequent click falls through to the session card behind it, triggering navigation.
30	 */
31	export function ResumeButton({
32	  sessionName,
33	  projectId,
34	  clientId,
35	  sessionDataSize,
36	  compact = false,
37	  className,
38	}: {
39	  sessionName: string;
40	  projectId?: string;
41	  clientId?: string;
42	  sessionDataSize?: number | null;
43	  compact?: boolean;
44	  className?: string;
45	}) {
46	  const resumeEnabled = useFlag("resume");
47	  const { can } = useEntitlement();
48	  const router = useRouter();
49	  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
50	  const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false);
51	
52	  if (!resumeEnabled) return null;
53	
54	  const isResumable = !!sessionDataSize && sessionDataSize > 0;
55	  const hasIds = !!projectId && !!clientId;
56	
57	  const handle = (e: React.MouseEvent) => {
58	    // Resume buttons sit inside clickable session cards/rows. Stop BOTH the React synthetic
59	    // event (so the card's onClick doesn't fire) and the native event (so document-level native
60	    // listeners don't see it) — the opening click must not navigate.
61	    e.preventDefault();
62	    e.stopPropagation();
63	    if (e.nativeEvent && typeof e.nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation === "function") {
64	      e.nativeEvent.stopImmediatePropagation();
65	    }
66	    if (!hasIds || !isResumable) return;
67	
68	    if (can("resume")) {
69	      // Copy inside the user-activation gesture (Safari-safe), then open the dialog deferred so
70	      // the overlay mounts AFTER this click's event chain resolves (prevents the click from
71	      // falling through to the card once the overlay unmounts on a later dismiss).
72	      void copyToClipboard(buildResumeCommand(projectId!, clientId!)).then((ok) => {
73	        if (ok) setCopied(true);
74	      });
75	      setTimeout(() => setOpen(true), 0);
76	    } else {
77	      router.push("/resume");
78	    }
79	  };
80	
81	  const close = () => {
82	    // Defer unmount so the dismiss event (overlay pointerdown / X click / Escape) fully
83	    // resolves against the still-mounted overlay before we tear the portal down — otherwise the
84	    // dismiss click can fall through to the session card behind it and trigger navigation.
85	    setTimeout(() => {
86	      setOpen(false);
87	      setCopied(false);
88	    }, 0);
89	  };
90	
91	  const tooltip = isResumable
92	    ? "Resume this session in an agent"
93	    : "This session predates resume support — re-sync it from its machine with a current CLI to enable.";
94	
95	  return (
96	    <>
97	      <Tooltip content={tooltip} side="bottom">
98	        <button
99	          type="button"
100	          onClick={handle}
101	          disabled={!isResumable}
102	          className={cn(
103	            "inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md text-xs font-medium transition-colors text-brand hover:bg-brand/10 disabled:opacity-40 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:hover:bg-transparent",
104	            compact ? "h-7 w-7 justify-center" : "h-7 px-2.5",
105	            className,
106	          )}
107	        >
108	          <RotateCcw size={14} className="flex-shrink-0" />
109	          {!compact && <span>Resume</span>}
110	        </button>
111	      </Tooltip>
112	      {open && hasIds && (
113	        <ResumeCommandDialog
114	          open={open}
115	          onClose={close}
116	          projectId={projectId!}
117	          sessionId={clientId!}
118	          sessionName={sessionName}
119	          initialCopied={copied}
120	        />
121	      )}
122	    </>
123	  );
124	}
125

**The bug fix — `ui-components/ui/dialog.tsx`:**

`DialogContent` now stops `click` propagation at the portal boundary, composed after the props spread so a consumer's own `onClick` still runs rather than clobbering it. The comment explains the actual mechanism (React bubbles synthetic events through the React tree, portals included, so the X click was reaching the card's `onClick`) with no doc references. It's deliberately click-only and content-only: stopping `pointerdown` would also halt the native event (React's `stopPropagation` stops both), hiding it from document-level listeners like Radix's own outside-dismiss detection — and the overlay is left alone for the same reason. Because this lives in the shared wrapper, **every** dialog rendered inside a clickable parent is now safe, not just this one.

**The cleanup it unlocked — `ResumeButton.tsx`:**

- `close()` is now a plain `setOpen(false); setCopied(false)` — the `setTimeout(0)` defer is gone (it never addressed the X leak anyway; the propagation path is fixed at dispatch time).

- `onInteractOutside={(e) => e.preventDefault()}` in `ResumeCommandDialog` is **kept** — that guards the second, distinct mechanism (Radix dismisses on pointerdown-outside; the unmounted overlay lets the follow-up click hit-test the card directly), which content-level `stopPropagation` cannot address.

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-14 20:40:49Z)**_

Here's each deferred item in full, with current locations and the concrete fix for each.

## CLI items

**(12) No logging in the URI-resolution path** — `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go` (zero `slog` calls in the file).
`resolveSessionURI` makes up to three consequential branch decisions — which URI form parsed, local hit vs. cloud, direct fetch vs. all-projects discovery — and none of them log. When a user reports "my pasted command says not found," `--debug` output shows nothing about where resolution looked or why it missed. Project convention is consistent observability via `log/slog`. Fix: `slog.Debug` at the decision points, e.g. after parse (`"resolved session URI", "form", "specstory|url|uuid", "project", pid`), on a local hit, on each cloud lookup, and on the final miss.

**(7) Circular help text** — `pkg/cmd/resume.go:83`.
The long description reads: *"…specstory:// URI (i.e. specstory://...), a cloud permalink, or a bare session UUID."* The parenthetical defines `specstory://` as `specstory://...` — it tells the reader nothing. Fix: show the actual shape, e.g. *"a specstory://projects/{id}/sessions/{id} URI, a cloud permalink, or a bare session UUID."*

**(10) Duplicated command tail** — `pkg/cmd/resume.go`, the `if sessionArg != ""` block (~24 lines).
The `--session`-without-agent sub-branch does `selectResumeViaTUI(...)` → `if err` → `if plan == nil` → `launchResume(...)`, which is character-for-character the same tail the default path below it runs — the only difference is passing `resolved` vs `nil` as the pinned session. Two copies of the same sequence will drift apart on the next change (e.g. someone adds a step to one and not the other). Fix: declare `var pinned *sessionindex.Session` before the block, have the `--session` branch just set it (and early-return only for the preset-agent case), and let both flows fall through to the single existing tail. Also restores the single-function-exit shape the conventions ask for.

**(17) Three lines duplicating `beginResume`** — `pkg/cmd/session_tui.go:276-278`.
The `pinnedSession` entry case sets `m.chosen` / `m.mode = modeTarget` / `m.targetCursor = m.defaultTargetIndex()` — the identical trio `beginResume` executes at lines ~997-998 when a session is picked in the browser. If target-picker entry ever grows a fourth step (say, an analytics ping or a validation), one of the two sites will be forgotten. Fix: extract a tiny `enterTargetPicker(sess *sessionindex.Session)` helper both call. Smallest item on the list; borderline not-worth-it, flagged for completeness.

**(43) Misleading not-found message** — `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go:223`.
`"session %s not found locally or in SpecStory Cloud"` is wrong in one real case: the session **is** in the cloud but has no `SessionData` blob (synced by an older CLI), so the `?resumable=true` listings can't see it. The web UI disables the Resume button for those, but a hand-pasted permalink or bare UUID hits this path and the user is told the session doesn't exist when it's sitting right there on cloud.specstory.com. Fix: extend the message, e.g. *"…not found locally or in SpecStory Cloud. If the session exists in the cloud, it may need re-syncing from its original machine with a current CLI."*

**(47) Fragile 403 detection** — `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go:300`.
`mapCloudResumeErr` decides "this is a Pro-gating failure" with `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "upgrade_required")`. That works because `skillsAPIRequest` (`pkg/cloud/skills.go:313-323`) surfaces the server's `{error: "..."}` envelope text verbatim and the server's `requireFeature` guard emits `upgrade_required` — but the HTTP status code is discarded in the process, so the CLI is string-matching on server copy. The day someone rewords that server message, non-Pro users stop getting *"Resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro."* and start seeing the raw server error instead — a silent regression no test will catch. Fix: have `skillsAPIRequest` return a typed error carrying the status code (mirroring how it already types 401 as `*ErrAuthenticationFailed`), and match `errors.As` + `StatusForbidden` in `mapCloudResumeErr`. This is the one I'd prioritize.

**(48) Same error, two spellings** — `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go:301` vs `pkg/cloud/resume_client.go:258`.
The resolution path says *"Resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro."* (capital R, trailing period); `FetchSessionData`'s 403 says *"resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro"*. Same condition, different user-visible text depending on **when** the 403 happens (during resolution vs. during the blob fetch). Trivial fix — one shared constant or matching strings — and it folds naturally into the (47) refactor.

**(52) Test gaps** — `pkg/cmd/session_uri_test.go` + `pkg/sessionindex`.
Three specific additions, all testing real logic:
- The parse table covers the `/chats/{id}` tail only for the `https` form — add the `specstory://` variant, since the custom-scheme path goes through the different host+path rejoin code before segment matching.
- No query-string case (`…/sessions/{sid}?foo=bar`). It passes today because `url.Parse` separates `RawQuery` from `Path`, but nothing pins that — a parser rewrite could regress it silently.
- `GetSessionByID`'s collision tiebreak (`pkg/sessionindex/store.go`): insert two rows sharing a `session_id` under different agents plus a soft-deleted third, assert the most-recent live row wins. That's the exact behavior the `ORDER BY updated_at DESC … LIMIT 1` + `deleted = 0` SQL encodes, and it's cheap with the store's existing test harness.

## Web items

**(W15) Inconsistent "Copied" indicator** — `ResumeCommandDialog.tsx`.
When the dialog opens, `useState(initialCopied)` shows "Copied" and it stays that way **forever** (until close). But clicking "Copy" again shows "Copied" for 2 seconds and then reverts to "Copy" — even though the clipboard content is identical in both cases. The same true state renders two different ways depending on how you got there. Fix: pick one behavior — either persist after manual copy too, or start the 2s revert timer on open as well.

**(W17) Dangling session name in the dialog text** — `ResumeCommandDialog.tsx`, the `DialogDescription`.
Renders as: *"Paste this command into a terminal on the computer where you want to continue the session. **My Session Name**"* — the bolded name trails the sentence as a floating fragment with no grammatical connection. Fix: weave it in, e.g. *"Paste this command into a terminal on the computer where you want to continue '**My Session Name**'."* (with a fallback sentence when the name is empty).

**(W18) Unverified docs link** — `ResumeCommandDialog.tsx`, the "SpecStory CLI" anchor.
It points at `https://docs.specstory.com/cloud/quickstart`. I never confirmed that page exists or that it's the CLI *installation* page rather than a general cloud quickstart — a user who clicks it needs install instructions specifically.
