Everything's implemented and green — CLI: `gofmt` clean, build OK, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, full test suite passes; web: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. All changes are uncommitted in both repos for you to review/commit.

First, your two questions:

**47 — "Why no real 403 response?!?"** The server *does* send a real 403 — the problem was CLI-side. `skillsAPIRequest` read `resp.StatusCode`, logged it, and then **threw it away**: it returned only the server's error *text* wrapped in a generic `error`, so by the time `mapCloudResumeErr` saw the error, the string was all that survived — hence the `strings.Contains("upgrade_required")` hack. Fixed properly: `skillsAPIRequest` now returns a typed `*cloud.APIError{StatusCode, Message}` for every non-2xx (message text unchanged, so nothing user-visible moved), and `mapCloudResumeErr` branches on `errors.As` + `http.StatusForbidden`. A server rewording can no longer silently break the Pro message.

**48 — you're half right.** The two strings differed in *both* the leading capital and the period: `"Resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro."` in `session_uri.go` vs `"resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro"` (lowercase r, no period) in `resume_client.go` — the lowercase one followed Go's error-string convention. Both now read identically: **"Resuming cloud sessions requires SpecStory Pro."** One wrinkle: `golangci-lint` (ST1005) rejects trailing punctuation in `fmt.Errorf`, so the `resume_client.go` one became an `APIError` struct literal instead — which is also just *correct* now, since it's a 403 and unifies with the (47) typed-error approach.

The rest, by number:

- **(12)** Six `slog.Debug` lines through `resolveSessionURI`: parsed form (`specstory`/`permalink`/`uuid`) + IDs, local-index hit, falling through to cloud, direct-form fallback scan, cross-project rejection, and the final miss. `--debug` now tells the whole resolution story.
- **(7)** Help text now reads "…a specstory:// URI, a cloud permalink, or a bare session UUID" — parenthetical gone.
- **(10)** `RunE` deduplicated: the `--session` branch now just sets a `pinned` variable (or early-returns for the preset-agent case) and falls through to the single shared `selectResumeViaTUI → launchResume` tail.
- **(17)** New `enterTargetPicker(sess)` helper in `session_tui.go`; both `beginResume` and the pinned-session entry case call it.
- **(43)** Message is now `"Resumable session %s not found locally or in SpecStory Cloud"`.
- **(52)** Three tests added: `specstory://` with a `/chats` tail (pins the custom scheme's separate host+path-rejoin parse path), an `https` permalink with a query string, and `TestGetSessionByID_MostRecentLiveRowWins` in `sessionindex` (collision tiebreak + soft-deleted rows never resolve).
- **(W15)** A single decay effect in the dialog: whenever `copied` becomes true — from copy-on-open or copy-again — it reverts to "Copy" after 2s. `copyAgain` lost its private timer.
- **(W17)** The description now reads *"…where you want to continue "My Session Name"."* with the name woven into the sentence, falling back to "the session" when unnamed.

180	// first-exchange lookup (sequential Supabase round-trips that would make the resume browse
181	// chronically slow on large projects; the CLI never uses exchangeCount/firstExchangeContent).
182	// Ordered by real activity (ended_at, then updated_at) so every resume surface sorts the same
183	// way. Callers add their own scoping (e.g. .limit()).
184	function resumableSessionsQuery(workspaceIds: string[]) {
185	  return supabaseClient()
186	    .from("sessions")
187	    .select(
188	      "id, client_id, workspace_id, name, user_title, markdown_size, raw_data_size, session_data_size, created_at, updated_at, started_at, ended_at, metadata"
189	    )
190	    .in("workspace_id", workspaceIds)
191	    .gt("session_data_size", 0)
192	    .order("ended_at", { ascending: false, nullsFirst: false })
193	    .order("updated_at", { ascending: false });
194	}
195	
196	// listWorkspacesWithResumableSessions returns the user's projects each carrying summaries of
197	// its cloud-resumable sessions inline (SessionSummary rows, not the SessionData blobs), for the
198	// CLI's all-projects browser rollup. Unlike listWorkspaces above,
199	// this groups per-session data so the CLI can dedup against its local index and recompute
200	// accurate per-agent chips + real activity dates client-side. Projects with no resumable
201	// sessions are dropped (no phantom zero-session rows). Deliberately no limit — accurate counts
202	// need every resumable session, and the fetch is a one-shot on entering the browser.
203	export async function listWorkspacesWithResumableSessions(
204	  request: ApiRequest
205	): Promise<Workspace[]> {
206	  const workspaceIds = await getAccessibleWorkspaceIds(request.userId!);
207	  if (workspaceIds.length === 0) {
208	    return [];
209	  }
210	
211	  // Workspace metadata (id/project_id/owner_id/name/icon/color) for the projects the sessions
212	  // roll up to.
213	  const { data: workspaces, error: wsError } = await supabaseClient()
214	    .from("workspaces")
215	    .select("id, project_id, owner_id, name, icon, color, created_at, updated_at")
216	    .in("id", workspaceIds);
217	  if (wsError && wsError.message) {
218	    throw new Error(`Failed to list workspaces: ${wsError.message}`);
219	  }
220	  if (!workspaces || workspaces.length === 0) {
221	    return [];
222	  }
223	
224	  const workspaceById = new Map<string, (typeof workspaces)[number]>();
225	  for (const w of workspaces) {
226	    workspaceById.set(w.id as string, w);
227	  }
228	
229	  // All resumable sessions across the user's workspaces in one query.
230	  const { data: sessions, error: sessError } =
231	    await resumableSessionsQuery(workspaceIds);
232	  if (sessError && sessError.message) {
233	    throw new Error(`Failed to list resumable sessions: ${sessError.message}`);
234	  }
235	  if (!sessions || sessions.length === 0) {
236	    return []; // no resumable sessions anywhere -> no projects to show from the cloud
237	  }
238	
239	  // Group sessions by workspace, then emit one Workspace per workspace that has sessions.
240	  // toSessionSummary takes the projectId; we resolve it from the workspace row (sessions have no
241	  // project_id column, only workspace_id).
242	  const sessionsByWorkspace = new Map<
243	    string,
244	    { projectId: string; sessions: SessionSummary[] }
245	  >();
246	  for (const session of sessions) {
247	    const workspaceId = session.workspace_id as string;
248	    const workspace = workspaceById.get(workspaceId);
249	    if (!workspace) {
250	      continue; // session's workspace not in the accessible set — skip (shouldn't happen)
251	    }
252	    const projectId = workspace.project_id as string;
253	    let bucket = sessionsByWorkspace.get(workspaceId);
254	    if (!bucket) {
255	      bucket = { projectId, sessions: [] };
256	      sessionsByWorkspace.set(workspaceId, bucket);
257	    }
258	    bucket.sessions.push(toSessionSummary(session, projectId, 0, ""));
259	  }
260	
261	  const out: Workspace[] = [];
262	  for (const [workspaceId, bucket] of sessionsByWorkspace) {
263	    const workspace = workspaceById.get(workspaceId)!;
264	    out.push({
265	      id: workspaceId,
266	      projectId: workspace.project_id as string,
267	      // From the workspace row, not request.userId: once team-visible workspaces land, the
268	      // accessible set includes workspaces the caller doesn't own.
269	      ownerId: workspace.owner_id as string,
270	      name: workspace.name as string,
271	      icon: (workspace.icon as string) || "FolderKanban",
272	      color: (workspace.color as string) || "blue",
273	      createdAt:
274	        (workspace.created_at as string) || new Date().toISOString(),
275	      updatedAt:
276	        (workspace.updated_at as string) || new Date().toISOString(),
277	      sessionCount: bucket.sessions.length,
278	      // Real activity across this project's resumable sessions — max of ended_at/started_at/updated_at
279	      // (NOT workspace.updated_at, which is the sync time). The CLI re-derives this per session anyway,
280	      // but lastUpdated is kept honest for any other consumer.
281	      lastUpdated: bucket.sessions.reduce((latest, s) => {
282	        const t = s.endedAt || s.startedAt || s.updatedAt;
283	        return t && (!latest || t > latest) ? t : latest;
284	      }, "" as string),
285	      sessions: bucket.sessions,
286	    });
287	  }
288	  return out;
289	}

300	  // read primitive.

305	    .eq("owner_id", request.userId!)
306	    .maybeSingle();

308	  if (ownErr || !owned) {
309	    throw new Error("You don't have permission to update this workspace");
310	  }
311	
312	  // Build update object with only provided fields
313	  const updateData: { icon?: string; color?: string; name?: string } = {};

_**Agent (claude-fable-5 2026-07-14 21:04:36Z)**_

Chunk 6 is implemented on both sides and verified — CLI: build, lint (0 issues), tests all pass; server: worker typecheck clean. All uncommitted for your review.

**Server (`specstory-sync`):**

- `worker/supabase.ts` — new `fetchAllResumableSessions` helper that drains `resumableSessionsQuery` in `.range()` pages of 1000 until a short page, with a comment explaining the trap it exists for (PostgREST silently truncates any un-ranged select at the Supabase "Max Rows" setting, so "no `.limit()`" was never actually unlimited). Both consumers now use it: `listResumableSessionsForWorkspace` (the `?resumable=true` per-project list — its `limit` parameter is gone) and `listWorkspacesWithResumableSessions` (the all-projects rollup — this also fixes the latent ~1000-row truncation that was quietly corrupting Chunk 4's rollup counts for heavy users).
- `worker/handlers/projects.ts` — the resumable branch calls without a limit; `limit` now applies only to the web app's ungated path, with a comment saying so.
- `worker/handlers/search.ts` + `shared/models/session.ts` — `RESUME_SEARCH_LIMIT` (500) deleted; `searchResumable` loses its `limit` parameter and the SQL `LIMIT` clause. No paging needed here: it's Drizzle straight to Postgres, so PostgREST's cap was never in play. The two-phase CTE still keeps `ts_headline` at one row per matched session, and the D21 watch item (headline cost on huge match sets) stands.

**CLI (`specstory-cli`):**

- `pkg/cloud/resume_client.go` — `cloudResumeLimit` deleted; `ListCloudSessions` sends `?resumable=true` with no `limit`; the `ListCloudSessions`/`SearchCloudSessions` doc comments now state the complete-set contract.
- `pkg/cmd/session_uri.go` — the direct-form fallback-to-anywhere branch (which existed purely to dodge the cap) is deleted along with its cross-project-rejection logic: a miss in the named project's now-complete list is genuinely not-found. `findCloudSessionInProject`'s comment updated to state the same contract.
- `docs/CLOUD-RESUME.md` — status line now marks Chunk 6 implemented, with the deploy constraint inline.

**Two operational notes:**

1. **Deploy order is load-bearing: server first.** A limit-less CLI request against the old server falls back to its default of **200** — worse than today's 500. The doc status line carries this warning.
2. The vitest suite in specstory-sync doesn't run in this checkout (`jsdom` missing from `node_modules` — all 6 test files fail to collect, pre-existing and unrelated); typecheck is the gate that ran.

Worth adding to the manual validation pass (per the doc's Chunk 6 list): a project with >1000 resumable sessions lists completely in browse and counts exactly in the rollup, a `--session` URI naming a very old session resolves with no fallback, and search latency stays acceptable on a large corpus.
